The Hàn clan then followed, not seeking the ancient teachings, Yíng Zhèng was imitated, the King’s networks and Emperor’s canons thus were quieted and not heard. The fading light was secluded and dark, the Way exhausted and fortunes shifted, Qián and Kūn cycled in calendar, selected the sagely and appointed the worthy, thus embracing the Greatly Departed, to entrust him with the numerous individuals. A dragon flying to initiate the blessings, in accord with the highest mysteries, the Five Transitions settled in order, he changed the title and revised the year, brilliant brilliant radiant radiant, he received the Mandate from Heaven. His benevolent air descended on all, virtue by ritual spread, his auspicious nature and sagely character, towering in youthful beauty. He mastered the Six Canons, learned without leaving the courtyard, devoted heart without fail, raising his will to the azure sky. Talent and refinement elegant and bright, like the luster of jade, he heard and discerned the soundless, gazed and saw the invisible. His firmness was like metal, his integrity like jasper, like the purity of ice, like the evenness of whetstones. He granted noble titles without bias, punished criminals without lenience, his heart reflected on all affairs, illuminated the feelings of those below. Wishing for good arms and legs [assistant ministers], praising the past’s Yī [Yǐn] and Lǚ [Shàng], he searched and raised up the low, citing [Shāng] Tāng and imitating [Xià] Yǔ, he drew out talents from mountain caves, chose servicemen from disheveled doors, only virtue was considered, no constraints by ancestry. On the surface of the settled land, morality and righteousness was his planning, not blocking away by rugged terrain, the Six Directions were his concern. Fair covenant was universally honored, below to purify the people, he expanded and developed standards and regulations, continuing on from predecessors. Law codes and rank systems, praised or censured by cause. He rode the chariots of Yīn, enacted the seasons of Xià. Gold Root Yellow Canopy, kingfisher feathers and dragon scales, robes and crown esteemed and beautiful, hanging tassels renewed, venerable and solemn in ritual expression, he appeared like a divinity. Regional governors wonderfully raised, reverent in sympathizing with the people, tiger officers carried insignia, defending the four borders. Wherever the vermilion flags cut down, the Nine Soils were shaken, who dared not comply, who dared not be a servant? Hanging banners by the sea, across ten thousand lǐ there was no dust. The caitiff [Liú] Bèi viciously pierced, birds falling at the Jiāng and Mín, [Sūn] Quán like a beached fish, dried and shriveled scales, the Sùshèn paid tribute, the Yuècháng delivered treasures, the Tiáozhī in cutoff regions sent sons as attendants to inwardly submit. Virtue comparable to the Former Imperials, achievements comparable to grand antiquity. The spirits above sent down signs, the Yellow Beginning [Huángchū] received the blessings, the Hé’s dragon and Luò’s turtle, crossed waves to roam downstream, level and balanced as measuring ropes, divine birds soared and danced, numerous jiá in the steps sprouted, restrained winds fanned away summer heat, white beasts and white birds, flew and ran in the suburbs and wilds, divine bells and treasure cauldrons, forms emerging from old earth, clouds blossoming sweet dew, rained and applied on the roofs, Língzhī grew in ponds, Zhūhuá shaded the shores. Swirling swirling the gentle wind, vast vast the sweet rain, sowed and reaped in abundance, our grain and our millet. Families girdled in the kindness of the lord, households immersed in the compassion of the father. He planned to deliver Grand Harmony, according with virtue and preserving righteousness, right about to ascend Jièshān, with the Former Imperial forming a pair, engraving stone to chronicle the merits, simultaneously recording the multitudes of omens, expanding the Fēng-Shàn [sacrifices], assigning the achievement to Heaven and Earth, host rituals for the hundred spirits, the standards of merit and fate observed, the Viewing Sacrifices to the Four Peaks, burning and conferring offered firewood, solemn in the South Suburbs, ancestral sacrifices to the Highest God, three sacrificial animals all provided, summer Dì autumn Cháng [sacrifices], inaugural lords accompanied in sacrifices, proffering jade rings and presenting jade tablets. Phoenix carriage shadowy and vast, dragon flag grand ceremonies, thus reaching Tài Temple, bells and drums sounded and sounded, eulogizing virtue and singing of achievement, eight rows of dancers swaying and swaying. The Imperial Ancestors thus fed, the illustrious father [Cáo Cāo] came to feast, the spirit satisfied and liquor finished, sending down good fortune. Heaven and Earth quaked and shook, so the Greatly Departed calmed them. The three celestials were dark and hidden, so the Greatly Departed illuminated them. The Imperial bonds were cut off, so the Greatly Departed weaved them. The Divine Vessels were not gathered, so the Greatly Departed managed them. Ritual and Music were neglected, so the Greatly Departed spread them. Benevolence and Righteousness were submerged, so the Greatly Departed raised them. Hidden Dragon Concealed Phoenix, so the Greatly Departed flew them. The distant Dí abandoned prosperity, so the Greatly Departed rectified them. On the Throne seven years, the foundational achievement was yet raised, about to have eternal Grand Harmony, surpassing the legacies of the Three [Augusts] and Five [Emperors], he should have been a teacher for all, expanding as a divine ruler, lifespan outlasting metal and stone, equaling the count of Dōngfù, how could he suddenly be lost, sending body to Lordly Earth, leaving us desolate desolate, without one to gaze to and without one to rely on. Oh august heavens, how can you be so cruel? Alas the Sorrow! Clearly investigating good or bad fortune, understanding from afar survival or destruction, he deeply passed down canon regulations, extending to the successor Imperial [Cáo Ruì]. The sagely ascended [Cáo Ruì] reverently serves [Cáo Pī’s Final Regulations], to follow and to enact, thus creates the Dark Rooms, foundation at Shǒuyáng, following the path of Gǔlín, recalling Yáo of admirable Táng, with the mountain sharing tomb, no trees no boundaries, pottery carriages and straw effigies, pearls and jade not stored. A hundred divinities alert in attention, coming guests in the secluded hall, farm birds field beasts, watch for the flight of the soul. Therefore, waiting for the great Passage’s completion, xī, selecting the auspicious time’s good fortune. Concealing flowery body in the catalpa coffin, xī, resting in the Main Hall to house the spirit. Looking back to the see the successor’s wails, xī, observing the attendees’ sorrowful sounds. Mourning that the Delayed Carriage is already prepared, xī, emotional at the Appearance Chariot’s fast journey. Floating the flying soul to the light clouds, xī, to the yellow ruins to extinguish the [bodily] form. Turning back on the Three Lights shining clear, xī, returning to the Dark Room’s gloomy depths. Oh once gone there is no return, xī, pained by the closed doors forever locked. Oh Your Distant Servant’s solitary distance, xī, moved by the horrific unspeakable to grief and shock. Heart isolated and cutoff with nowhere to express [my sorrow], xī, numerous flowing tears crossing the neck. Pondering your grace and glory to rashly run [to you], xī, obstructed by the gate passes’ lofty towers. Looking back to my mourning sash to recklessly set out, xī, constrained by the passes binding me. Wishing to fly high and distantly rest [at your tomb], xī, fearing the far spread of Heaven’s Net. Distantly throwing my bones to the foot of your mountain, xī, to repay your kindness and nurture in the Lower Court. Indignantly beating chest and self-lamenting, xī, fearing that your bestowals were heavy and my life is light. Sighing, the trifling drive to action, xī, sweetly willing for nine deaths and forgetting life. Almost in the director of life’s conscription registers, xī, before the yellow haired to fall and wither. Heaven covers high but examines the low, xī, I hope that the divine intelligence listens to us. Alone and desolate but with none to tell, xī, I look back to my shadow and pity the form. Presenting this document to write thoughts, xī, I join brush and ink to lay out my sincerity. Alas the Sorrow!’”



〔二〕　魏氏春秋曰：明帝將送葬，曹真、陳群、王朗等以暑熱固諫，乃止。孫盛曰：夫窀穸之事，孝子之極痛也，人倫之道，於斯莫重。故天子七月而葬，同軌畢至。夫以義感之情，猶盡臨隧之哀，況乎天性發中，敦禮者重之哉！魏氏之德，仍世不基矣。昔華元厚葬，君子以為棄君於惡，群等之諫，棄孰甚焉！鄄城侯植為誄曰：「惟黃初七年五月七日，大行皇帝崩，嗚呼哀哉！于時天震地駭，崩山隕霜，陽精薄景，五緯錯行，百姓呼嗟，萬國悲傷，若喪考妣，（恩過慕）〔思慕過〕唐，擗踊郊野，仰想穹蒼，僉曰何辜，早世殞喪，嗚呼哀哉！悲夫大行，忽焉光滅，永棄萬國，雲往雨絕。承問荒忽，惛懵哽咽，袖鋒抽刃，歎自僵斃，追慕三良，甘心同穴。感惟南風，惟以鬱滯，終於偕沒，指景自誓。考諸先記，尋之哲言，生若浮寄，唯德可論，朝聞夕逝，孔志所存。皇雖一沒，天祿永延，何以述德？表之素旃。何以詠功？宣之管絃。乃作誄曰：皓皓太素，兩儀始分，中和產物，肇有人倫，爰暨三皇，實秉道真，降逮五帝，繼以懿純，三代制作，踵武立勳。季嗣不維，網漏于秦，崩樂滅學，儒坑禮焚，二世而殲，漢氏乃因，弗求古訓，嬴政是遵，王綱帝典，闃爾無聞。末光幽昧，道究運遷，乾坤迴曆，簡聖授賢，乃眷大行，屬以黎元。龍飛啟祚，合契上玄，五行定紀，改號革年，明明赫赫，受命于天。仁風偃物，德以禮宣；祥惟聖質，嶷在幼妍。庶幾六典，學不過庭，潛心無罔，抗志青冥。才秀藻朗，如玉之瑩，聽察無嚮，瞻睹未形。其剛如金，其貞如瓊，如冰之潔，如砥之平。爵公無私，戮違無輕，心鏡萬機，攬照下情。思良股肱，嘉昔伊、呂，搜揚側陋，舉湯代禹；拔才巖穴，取士蓬戶，唯德是縈，弗拘禰祖。宅土之表，道義是圖，弗營厥險，六合是虞。齊契共遵，下以純民，恢拓規矩，克紹前人。科條品制，褒貶以因。乘殷之輅，行夏之辰。金根黃屋，翠葆龍鱗，紼冕崇麗，衡紞維新，尊肅禮容，矚之若神。方牧妙舉，欽於恤民，虎將荷節，鎮彼四鄰；朱旗所剿，九壤被震，疇克不若？孰敢不臣？縣旌海表，萬里無塵。虜備凶徹，鳥殪江岷，權若涸魚，乾腊矯鱗，肅慎納貢，越裳效珍，條支絕域，侍子內賓。德儕先皇，功侔太古。上靈降瑞，黃初叔祜：河龍洛龜，淩波游下；平鈞應繩，神鸞翔舞；數莢階除，系風扇暑；皓獸素禽，飛走郊野；神鍾寶鼎，形自舊土；雲英甘露，瀸塗被宇；靈芝冒沼，朱華蔭渚。回回凱風，祁祁甘雨，稼穡豐登，我稷我黍。家佩惠君，戶蒙慈父。圖致太和，洽德全義。將登介山，先皇作儷。鐫石紀勳，兼錄眾瑞，方隆封禪，歸功天地，賓禮百靈，勳命視規，望祭四嶽，燎封奉柴，肅于南郊，宗祀上帝。三牲既供，夏禘秋嘗，元侯佐祭，獻璧奉璋。鸞輿幽藹，龍旂太常，爰迄太廟，鍾鼓鍠鍠，頌德詠功，八佾鏘鏘。皇祖既饗，烈考來享，神具醉止，降茲福祥。天地震蕩，大行康之；三辰暗昧，大行光之；皇紘絕維，大行綱之；神器莫統，大行當之；禮樂廢弛，大行張之；仁義陸沈，大行揚之；潛龍隱鳳，大行翔之；疏狄遐康，大行匡之。在位七載，元功仍舉，將永太和，絕跡三五，宜作物師，長為神主，壽終金石，等算東父，如何奄忽，摧身后土，俾我〈煢，去冖〉〈煢，去冖〉，靡瞻靡顧。嗟嗟皇穹，胡寧忍務？嗚呼哀哉！明監吉凶，體遠存亡，深垂典制，申之嗣皇。聖上虔奉，是順是將，乃創玄宇，基為首陽，擬跡穀林，追堯慕唐，合山同陵，不樹不疆，塗車芻靈，珠玉靡藏。百神警侍，來賓幽堂，耕禽田獸，望魂之翔。於是，俟大隧之致功兮，練元辰之淑禎，潛華體於梓宮兮，馮正殿以居靈。顧望嗣之號咷兮，存臨者之悲聲，悼晏駕之既脩兮，感容車之速征。浮飛魂於輕霄兮，就黃墟以滅形，背三光之昭晰兮，歸玄宅之冥冥。嗟一往之不反兮，痛閟闥之長扃。咨遠臣之眇眇兮，感凶諱以怛驚，心孤絕而靡告兮，紛流涕而交頸。思恩榮以橫奔兮，閡闕塞之嶢崢，顧衰絰以輕舉兮，迫關防之我嬰。欲高飛而遙憩兮，憚天網之遠經，遙投骨於山足兮，報恩養於下庭。慨拊心而自悼兮，懼施重而命輕，嗟微驅之是效兮，甘九死而忘生，幾司命之役籍兮，先黃髮而隕零，天蓋高而察卑兮，冀神明之我聽。獨鬱伊而莫愬兮，追顧景而憐形，奏斯文以寫思兮，結翰墨以敷誠。嗚呼哀哉！」







Previously, the Emperor enjoyed literary scholarship, attended to writing and composition, what he personally collated and completed was bequeathed as a hundred volumes. He also employed various classicists to compile the classics and commentaries, by their type joined with one another, altogether over a thousand volumes, titled as the Huánglǎn. [46]



初，帝好文學，以著述為務，自所勒成垂百篇。又使諸儒撰集經傳，隨類相從，凡千餘篇，號曰皇覽。〔一〕










[46] Wèi shū states: When the Emperor was previously at the East Palace, an epidemic greatly rose, at the time people suffered and died. The Emperor was deeply emotional and sighed, and to Minister Judge Wáng Lǎng, whom he always respected, wrote a letter that said: “Living, there is seven chǐ of body. Dead, there is only one coffin of soil. Only by establishing virtue and raising reputation can there be no decay. After that there is nothing as good as writing books. Epidemics have repeatedly risen, servicemen and people dying and falling. I alone am what man, to be able to preserve this lifespan?” Therefore he considered and compiled what he had written, the Diǎnlùn, poems, rhapsodies, altogether over a hundred volumes, gathered various classicists within Sùchéng’s gates, discussing and debating great meanings, consistently without tiring. He always praised Hàn Emperor Wén’s conduct as a lord, lenient and benevolent, mysterious and silent, attending to the desire to influence the people by virtue, having the airs of a worthy sage. At the time of the literary scholars and various classicists, some believed that although Xiào-Wén was worthy, his intelligence and understanding of state systems did not compare to Jiǎ Yì. The Emperor because of this wrote the Tàizōng Lùn stating: “In the past Yǒu Miáo did not submit and Chónghuá danced with shield and battle-axe, Wèi Tuó declared himself Emperor and Xiào-Wén succored him with merciful virtue, the King of Wú did not attend Court, [Xiào-Wén] bestowed him with table and cane to succor his thoughts, and Heaven’s Under depended on this for calm. Thus he spread the teachings of the Three Clauses, the influence of contentedness and fraternity, wishing to allow those people who in past times accumulated fatigue, to be able to stride forward and openly discuss without fearful hearts. Something like Jiǎ Yì’s talent and cleverness, planning and preparing state government, is only the talent of a worthy minister, the quality of Guǎn [Zhòng] and Yàn [Yīng]. How could it compare to Xiào-Wén’s capacity as a great man?” During the Third Year, as Sūn Quán would not submit, he again issued Tàizōng Lùn to Heaven’s Under, to clearly show that he had not wanted to go to war. On another day he also casually said: “Looking back, I also have three matters that I cannot seek to imitate from Hàn Emperor Wén: killing Bó Zhāo, favoring Dèng Tōng, and having the consort Shèn wear clothes that did not touch the ground and gather up document bags to make curtains. I believe that Hàn Wén’s frugality was beyond propriety. To the family of his mother’s brother, he should have only cared for them with favor and should not have lent them authority, so that they violated criminal law and also could not but come to harm.” His desire was to maintain the center way, believing that Emperors and Kings in bearing should be like this.
Hú Chōng’s Wú lì states: The Emperor had a silk book of his composed Diǎnlùn and poems and rhapsodies gifted to Sūn Quán, and also had a paper copy sent to Zhāng Zhāo.



〔一〕　魏書曰：帝初在東宮，疫癘大起，時人彫傷，帝深感歎，與素所敬者大理王朗書曰：「生有七尺之形，死唯一棺之土，唯立德揚名，可以不朽，其次莫如著篇籍。疫癘數起，士人彫落，余獨何人，能全其壽？」故論撰所著典論、詩賦，蓋百餘篇，集諸儒於肅城門內，講論大義，侃侃無倦。常嘉漢文帝之為君，寬仁玄默，務欲以德化民，有賢聖之風。時文學諸儒，或以為孝文雖賢，其於聰明，通達國體，不如賈誼。帝由是著太宗論曰：「昔有苗不賓，重華舞以干戚，尉佗稱帝，孝文撫以恩德，吳王不朝，錫之几杖以撫其意，而天下賴安；乃弘三章之教，愷悌之化，欲使曩時累息之民，得闊步高談，無危懼之心。若賈誼之才敏，籌畫國政，特賢臣之器，管、晏之姿，豈若孝文大人之量哉？」三年之中，以孫權不服，復頒太宗論于天下，明示不願征伐也。他日又從容言曰：「顧我亦有所不取于漢文帝者三：殺薄昭；幸鄧通；慎夫人衣不曳地，集上書囊為帳帷。以為漢文儉而無法，舅后之家，但當養育以恩而不當假借以權，既觸罪法，又不得不害矣。」其欲秉持中道，以為帝王儀表者如此。胡沖吳曆曰：帝以素書所著典論及詩賦餉孫權，又以紙寫一通與張昭。







Appraisal States: Emperor Wén was naturally endowed with literary elegance, on using brush completed a work, widely learned and strong memory, talents and arts both furnished. [47] If only he had added to it an expansive and broad tolerance, strove with fair and impartial sincerity, chased his ambitions while preserving the way, achieved and expanded a virtuous heart, then compared to the worthy rulers of antiquity, how would there be such a distance?



評曰：文帝天資文藻，下筆成章，博聞彊識，才蓺兼該；〔一〕若加之曠大之度，勵以公平之誠，邁志存道，克廣德心，則古之賢主，何遠之有哉！










[47] (1) In Diǎnlùn the Emperor’s Self Narration states: In Chūpíng’s Inaugural [190], Dǒng Zhuó killed the Ruler and poisoned the [Dowager] Empress, overthrew and overturned the Ruling House. At the time the Four Seas were already destitute from the government of Zhōngpíng [184 - 189], and further loathing [Dǒng] Zhuó’s vicious rebellion, family after family worried of chaos, man after man feared themselves in danger. East of the mountains the Governors and Administrators all used the Chūnqiū’s principle of “Wèi men suppressed Zhōuyù at Pú” to say that man after man all were able to suppress rebels. Thereupon there was a great raising of Righteous Troops, famed heroes and great vigilantes, wealthy houses and powerful clans, whirling and rising like clouds gathering, ten thousand lǐ joining one another. The brigades of Yǎn and Yù [Provinces] battled at Xíngyáng, the armor of Hénèi militarized Mèngjīn. [Dǒng] Zhuó therefore moved the Great Carriage, shifting the capital west to Cháng’ān. And so east of the mountains, the large linked prefectures and states, the middle fortified cities and towns, the small assembled paths and streets, in turn swallowing and exterminating one another. It happened the Huángjīn flourished in Hǎi and Dài, mountain bandits were violent in Bìng and Jì [Provinces], riding victories to turn and attack, engulfing and going south. Villages and cities spotted smoke and fled, city walls saw dust [of approaching armies] and dispersed, the Hundred Surnames perished and died, exposed bones like weeds. At the time I was aged five years, and my father, because the world was disturbed and in chaos, taught me to learn to shoot. At six years I knew how to shoot, and he also taught me to ride horse. At eight years I was able to ride and shoot. Because at the time there were many dangers, in every campaign I always accompanied. At Jiàn’ān’s beginning [196], my father campaigned south against Jīng Province, reaching Wǎn, and Zhāng Xiù surrendered. Within ten days he rebelled, and I lost my elder brother the Filial-Incorruptible [Cáo Áng] Zǐxiū, and my elder cousin Ānmín came to harm. At the time I was aged ten years, and rode horse to escape. The ways of the civil and military, each according to the times are used. I was born at the end of Zhōngpíng [184 – 189], grew up among weapons and soldiers, and therefore from youth enjoyed the bow and horse, and to now I have not declined, chasing game for ten lǐ, galloping and shooting always at a hundred bù, the days many and body strong, my heart never tired of it. Jiàn’ān Tenth Year [205], having just settled Jì Province, the Huìmò sent tribute of excellent bows, Yān and Dài proffered famed horses. At the time it was the end of spring, Gōumáng directing the season, mild breeze fanning things, bow dry and hand supple, grass shallow and beasts fat, with my elder cousin Zǐdān we hunted to Yè’s west, at the end of the day we hand captured deer of nine, pheasants and hares of thirty. Later the army campaigned south and stopped at Qǔlí, Secretariat Writers Director Xún Yù served a mission to present comforts to the army, and after meeting and conversing with me, [Xún] Yù said: “I have heard that you are skilled at shooting with both left and right. This is a truly difficult ability.” I said: “Your Honor has not yet seen launching from neck and unleashing by mouth, bending down to the horse hooves and looking up to the targets.” [Xún] Yù laughed and said: “Really then?” I said: “The [archery] range has a constant track; the targets have designated places. Even if every shot be a hit, it is not utmost mastery. But riding on open plains, racing across dense grasses, pursuing cunning beasts, intercepting light birds, ensuring the bow never be bent in vain, every shot certain to pierce through, then that would be mastery.” At the time Army Libationer Zhāng Jīng was seated, and looking to [Xún] Yù clapped his hands and said: “Excellent!” I also learned sword fencing, and studied many masters, across the Four Quarters the techniques are each unique, but only the masters of the capital are the best. During the times of Huán and Líng, there was a Tiger Elite Wáng Yuè who excelled in these techniques, and was praised by the capital masters. Hénán’s Shǐ Ā said that he in the past traveled with [Wáng] Yuè, completely learned his methods, and I studied under [Shǐ] Ā to learn its essential skills. Once I was with Pacifying Caitiffs General Liú Xūn and Exerting Authority General Dèng Zhǎn and others together drinking. Previously I had heard that [Dèng] Zhǎn was strong in arm, had learned the Five Weapons, and also had been praised as being able to use bare hands against naked blades. I discussed swords with him for a good while, and said that the General’s skills were not as said, that I had always enjoyed these things, and also had obtained excellent skills, and therefore asked him to face me. At the time we were so intoxicated that our ears burned, and just happened to be eating sugar canes, so we used them as sticks, went down from the Hall and repeatedly sparred, three times striking his arm, and those left and right greatly laughed. [Dèng] Zhǎn was dissatisfied, and requested to go again. I said that my technique was of a fast sort, difficult to use to strike the face, and therefore only struck the arms. [Dèng] Zhǎn said he wished to spar one more time. I knew he wished to charge to seek to engage the center and therefore feigned a deep advance. [Dèng] Zhǎn indeed charged ahead, but I on merely pulling back my leg struck right on his forehead, and those seated and watching were startled. I returned to my seat, and laughed and said: “In the past Yáng Qīng had Chúnyú Yì abandon his former methods, and again receive instruction in secret techniques. Now I also wish for General Dèng [Zhǎn] to abandon his former tricks, and again receive instruction on the important principles.” All those seated were thoroughly entertained. [But] in such matters, one cannot really call oneself great. When young I learned dual wielding, and myself said that I was without match. Commonly dual halberds are called ‘sitting in iron chamber,’ side shields are called ‘the covering wooden door.’ Later I studied under Chén state’s Yuán Mǐn, who used one [weapon] to fight dual [wielding], in every match he was like a spirit, the opponent did not know where he would strike out. In those former days if I had encountered [Yuán] Mǐn on a narrow road, [the duel] would have at once be decided [against me]! With other games I had few that I enjoyed, only in playing Dànqí was I somewhat thorough in the skill, and when young made a rhapsody for it. In the past in the capital the foremost players were Mǎ the Marquess of Hé village, Dōngfāng Ānshì, and young noble Zhāng, and I always regret that I could not have played against these masters. My father greatly enjoyed the Shī [jīng] and [Shàng] Shū and literature. Although he was in the army, his hands did not set aside books, and always studied them when at ease, always saying: “Men who are studious when young are able to think hard, but when grown are forgetful. Those grown up but still able to be diligent in study are only me and Yuán Bóyè.” I therefore when young recited [from memory] the Shī [jīng] and Lún [yǔ], and when grown studied through the words of the Five Classics, the Four Genres, the Shǐ[jì] and Hàn[shū], and the Hundred Schools of thought, and there was none I did not read.
Bówùzhì states: The Emperor was skilled in Dànqí, able to use a hand towel’s corner. At the time there was a scholar, also able to lower his head to use his cap’s hemp headscarf corner to cast the pieces.



〔一〕　典論帝自敘曰：初平之元，董卓殺主鴆后，蕩覆王室。是時四海既困中平之政，兼惡卓之凶逆，家家思亂，人人自危。山東牧守，咸以春秋之義，「衛人討州吁于濮」，言人人皆得討賊。於是大興義兵，名豪大俠，富室強族，飄揚雲會，萬里相赴；兗、豫之師戰于滎陽，河內之甲軍于孟津。卓遂遷大駕，西都長安。而山東大者連郡國，中者嬰城邑，小者聚阡陌，以還相吞滅。會黃巾盛於海、岱，山寇暴於并、冀，乘勝轉攻，席卷而南，鄉邑望煙而奔，城郭睹塵而潰，百姓死亡，暴骨如莽。余時年五歲，上以世方擾亂，教余學射，六歲而知射，又教余騎馬，八歲而能騎射矣。以時之多故，每征，余常從。建安初，上南征荊州，至宛，張繡降。旬日而反，亡兄孝廉子修、從兄安民遇害。時余年十歲，乘馬得脫。夫文武之道，各隨時而用，生于中平之季，長于戎旅之間，是以少好弓馬，于今不衰；逐禽輒十里，馳射常百步，日多體健，心每不厭。建安十年，始定冀州，濊、貊貢良弓，燕、代獻名馬。時歲之暮春，勾芒司節，和風扇物，弓燥手柔，草淺獸肥，與族兄子丹獵于鄴西，終日手獲獐鹿九，雉兔三十。後軍南征次曲蠡，尚書令荀彧奉使犒軍，見余談論之末，彧言：「聞君善左右射，此實難能。」余言：「執事未睹夫項發口縱，俯馬蹄而仰月支也。」彧喜笑曰：「乃爾！」余曰：「埒有常徑，的有常所，雖每發輒中，非至妙也。若馳平原，赴豐草，要狡獸，截輕禽，使弓不虛彎，所中必洞，斯則妙矣。」時軍祭酒張京在坐，顧彧拊手曰「善」。余又學擊劍，閱師多矣，四方之法各異，唯京師為善。桓、靈之間，有虎賁王越善斯術，稱於京師。河南史阿言昔與越遊，具得其法，余從阿學之精熟。嘗與平虜將軍劉勳、奮威將軍鄧展等共飲，宿聞展善有手臂，曉五兵，又稱其能空手入白刃。余與論劍良久，謂言將軍法非也，余顧嘗好之，又得善術，因求與余對。時酒酣耳熱，方食芊蔗，便以為杖，下殿數交，三中其臂，左右大笑。展意不平，求更為之。余言吾法急屬，難相中面，故齊臂耳。展言願復一交，余知其欲突以取交中也，因偽深進，展果尋前，余卻腳鄛，正截其顙，坐中驚視。余還坐，笑曰：「昔陽慶使淳于意去其故方，更授以祕術，今余亦願鄧將軍捐棄故伎，更受要道也。」一坐盡歡。夫事不可自謂己長，余少曉持複，自謂無對；俗名雙戟為坐鐵室，鑲楯為蔽木戶；後從陳國袁敏學，以單攻複，每為若神，對家不知所出，先日若逢敏於狹路，直決耳！余於他戲弄之事少所喜，唯彈棋略盡其巧，少為之賦。昔京師先工有馬合鄉侯、東方安世、張公子，常恨不得與彼數子者對。上雅好詩書文籍，雖在軍旅，手不釋卷，每每定省從容，常言人少好學則思專，長則善忘，長大而能勤學者，唯吾與袁伯業耳。余是以少誦詩、論，及長而備歷五經、四部，史、漢、諸子百家之言，靡不畢覽。博物志曰：帝善彈棋，能用手巾角。時有一書生，又能低頭以所冠著葛巾角撇棋。

title: 3  Annals of Emperor Míng
3  Annals of Emperor Míng
text:
Míng Huángdì forbidden name Ruì, appellation Yuánzhòng, was Wén-dì’s [Cáo Pī] Heir-Apparent. When he was born Tàizǔ [Cáo Cāo] favored him, always having him among his Left and Right. [1] Aged fifteen years, enfeoffed as Marquess of Wǔdé. Huángchū Second Year, became Duke of Qí, Third Year, became King of Píngyuán. As his mother was executed, therefore he was not yet established as the successor. [2] Seventh Year, Summer, Fifth Moon [226 Jun 13 – Jul 11], the Emperor was critically ill, and so enthroned him as Imperial Heir-Apparent. Dīngsì [226 Jun 29], succeeded the Imperial Emperor’s throne, Great Amnesty. Honored the Imperial Dowager Empress as Grand Imperial Dowager Empress, Imperial Empress as Imperial Dowager Empress. The various ministers were enfeoffed with noble ranks each on distinct basis. [3] Guǐwèi [226 Jul 25], posthumously titled his mother the consort Zhēn as Wén-Zhāo Huánghòu. Rénchén [226 Aug 3], enthroned the Imperial younger brother [Cáo] Ruí as King of Yángpíng.



明皇帝諱叡，字元仲，文帝太子也。生而太祖愛之，常令在左右。〔一〕年十五，封武德侯，黃初二年為齊公，三年為平原王。以其母誅，故未建為嗣。〔二〕七年夏五月，帝病篤，乃立為皇太子。丁巳，即皇帝位，大赦。尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。諸臣封爵各有差。〔三〕癸未，追諡母甄夫人曰文昭皇后。壬辰，立皇弟蕤為陽平王。










[1] Wèi shū states: The Emperor was several years old and had appearance of precocious intelligence, Wǔ Huángdì [Cáo Cāo] was impressed with him, and said: “Our foundation due to you is three generations.” At every Court and feast gathering, he was with the Attendant Centrals and close ministers together lined within the curtains. He enjoyed study and remembered much, and especially devoted attention on legal principles.



〔一〕　魏書曰：帝生數歲而有岐嶷之姿，武皇帝異之，曰：「我基於爾三世矣。」每朝宴會同，與侍中近臣並列帷幄。好學多識，特留意於法理。













[2] Wèi lüè states: Emperor Wén, because the empress Guō had no children, had Edict for her adopt and raise the Emperor. The Emperor because his mother had not ended well was extremely indignant in thought. Later he could not obtain his wishes, and so respectfully served the empress Guō, morning and evening using the Chief Managers to ask after her rising and resting. The empress Guō also because she had no children therefore applied parental affection on him. Emperor Wén originally, because the Emperor had been displeased, had intention and wish for another concubine’s son the King of Jīngzhào [Cáo Lǐ] to become successor, and therefore for a long time did not appoint an Heir-Apparent.
Wèi Mò zhuàn states: The Emperor once accompanied Emperor Wén in a hunt, seeing a child and mother deer. Emperor Wén shot and killed the mother deer, and ordered the Emperor shoot the child deer. The Emperor did not obey, saying: “Your Majesty has already killed its mother, Your Servant cannot bear to further kill its child.” Therefore he shed tears. Emperor Wén at once dropped his bow and arrows, because of this was deeply surprised of him, and so his intentions on the establishment were settled.



〔二〕　魏略曰：文帝以郭后無子，詔使子養帝。帝以母不以道終，意甚不平。後不獲已，乃敬事郭后，旦夕因長御問起居，郭后亦自以無子，遂加慈愛。文帝始以帝不悅，有意欲以他姬子京兆王為嗣，故久不拜太子。魏末傳曰：帝常從文帝獵，見子母鹿。文帝射殺鹿母，使帝射鹿子，帝不從，曰：「陛下已殺其母，臣不忍復殺其子。」因涕泣。文帝即放弓箭，以此深奇之，而樹立之意定。













[3] Shìyǔ states: The Emperor and the Court servicemen had previously not interacted. After he ascended the throne, the various subordinates wanted to know of his mannerisms. After a few days, he met alone with Attendant Central Liú Yè, conversing all day. Everyone leaned in to listen. When [Liú] Yè exited, they asked: “What is he like?” [Liú] Yè said: “A peer of Qín Shǐhuáng and Hàn Xiào-Wǔ, the gap in talent is miniscule.



〔三〕　世語曰：帝與朝士素不接，即位之後，群下想聞風采。居數日，獨見侍中劉曄，語盡日。眾人側聽，曄既出，問「何如」？曄曰：「秦始皇、漢孝武之儔，才具微不及耳。」







Eighth Moon [226 Sep 10 – Oct 8], Sūn Quán attacked Jiāngxià prefecture, the Administrator Wén Pìn firmly defended. The Court discussed wishing to mobilize soldiers to rescue it. The Emperor said: “[Sūn] Quán is accustomed to river battle. That he dares dismount his boats to attack on land is only to surprise attack the unprepared. Now he is already locked together with [Wén] Pìn, attackers must be several times stronger than defenders, so in the end he will not dare remain long.” Before that time he had sent Managing Documents Attendant Censor Xún Yǔ to show appreciations for labors on the border regions. [Xún] Yǔ arrived at Jiāngxià and mobilized the soldiers of the counties he passed through and his accompanying infantry and cavalry of a thousand men to climb up the mountains and light fires. [Sūn] Quán retreated and fled.



八月，孫權攻江夏郡，太守文聘堅守。朝議欲發兵救之，帝曰：「權習水戰，所以敢下船陸攻者，幾掩不備也。今已與聘相持，夫攻守勢倍，終不敢久也。」先時遣治書侍御史荀禹慰勞邊方，禹到，於江夏發所經縣兵及所從步騎千人乘山舉火，權退走。




Xīnsì [226 Sep 21], established the Imperial son [Cáo] Jiǒng as King of Qīnghé. Wú officers Zhūgě Jǐn, Zhāng Bà, and others plundered Xiāngyáng. Succoring Army General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng suppressed and defeated them, beheaded [Zhāng] Bà. Campaigning East General-in-Chief Cáo Xiū also defeated their separate officers at Xúnyáng. Discussed the achievements and enacted rewards each on distinct basis. Winter, Tenth Moon [226 Nov 8 – Dec 6], the King of Qīnghé [Cáo] Jiǒng died. Twelfth Moon [227 Jan 6 – Feb 3], appointed Grand Commandant Zhōng Yáo as Grand Tutor, Campaigning East General-in-Chief Cáo Xiū as Marshal-in-Chief, Central Army General-in-Chief Cáo Zhēn as General-in-Chief, Excellency over the Masses Huà Xīn as Grand Commandant, Excellency of Works Wáng Lǎng as Excellency over the Masses, Defending Army General-in-Chief Chén Qún as Excellency of Works, Succoring Army General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng as Agile Cavalry General-in-Chief.



辛巳，立皇子冏為清河王。吳將諸葛瑾、張霸等寇襄陽，撫軍大將軍司馬宣王討破之，斬霸，征東大將軍曹休又破其別將於尋陽。論功行賞各有差。冬十月，清河王冏薨。十二月，以太尉鍾繇為太傅，征東大將軍曹休為大司馬，中軍大將軍曹真為大將軍，司徒華歆為太尉，司空王朗為司徒，鎮軍大將軍陳群為司空，撫軍大將軍司馬宣王為驃騎大將軍。




Tàihé Inaugural Year, Spring, Standard Moon [227 Feb 4 – Mar 5], Suburb Sacrifices to Wǔ Huángdì to match with Heaven, Ancestral Sacrifices to Wén Huángdì in Míngtáng to match with Highest God. Divided Jiāngxià’s southern part, installed a Jiāngxià Southern Division Commandant. Xīpíng’s Qū Yīng rebelled, killed the Línqiāng Magistrate and Xīdū Chief. Sent Generals Hǎo Zhāo and Lù Pán to suppress and beheaded him. Second Moon [227 Mar 6 – Apr 3], Xīnwèi [227 Mar 10], the Emperor plowed the Register Field. Xīnsì [227 Mar 20], established Wén-Zhāo Huánghòu’s tomb and temple at Yè. Dīnghài [227 Mar 26], Morning Sun in the East Suburbs. Summer, Fourth Moon [227 May 4 – Jun 1], enacted the wǔzhū coinage. Jiǎshēn [227 May 22], began construction of the Ancestral Temple. Autumn, Eighth Moon [227 Aug 30 – Sep 27], Evening Moon in the West Suburbs. Winter, Tenth Moon [227 Oct 28 – Nov 26], Bǐngyín [227 Oct 31], Drilled Troops in the East Suburbs. The King of Yānqí sent a son to enter as an attendant. Eleventh Moon [227 Nov 27 – Dec 25], enthroned as Imperial Empress Máo-shì. Bestowed on Heaven’s Under’s adult males noble rank at level two, the widowers and widows and orphans and childless and those unable to support themselves were bestowed grain. Twelfth Moon [227 Dec 26 – 228 Jan 24], enfeoffed the Empress’s father Máo Jiā as a Ranked Marquess. Xīnchéng Administrator Mèng Dá rebelled, Edict on Agile Cavalry General Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng to suppress him. [4]



太和元年春正月，郊祀武皇帝以配天，宗祀文皇帝於明堂以配上帝。分江夏南部，置江夏南部都尉。西平麴英反，殺臨羌令、西都長，遣將軍郝昭、鹿磐討斬之。二月辛未，帝耕於籍田。辛巳，立文昭皇后寢廟於鄴。丁亥，朝日于東郊。夏四月乙亥，行五銖錢。甲申，初營宗廟。秋八月，夕月于西郊。冬十月丙寅，治兵于東郊。焉耆王遣子入侍。十一月，立皇后毛氏。賜天下男子爵人二級，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者賜穀。十二月，封后父毛嘉為列侯。新城太守孟達反，詔驃騎將軍司馬宣王討之。〔一〕










[4] Sānfǔ Juélù states: Bóláng, Liáng province man, his reputation not good.
Its annotation states: Bóláng was surnamed Mèng, personal name Tā, a Fúfēng man. In Emperor Líng’s time, Central Regular Attendant Zhāng Ràng controlled the Court and government, [Zhāng] Ràng’s supervisor slave managed and protected household affairs. [Mèng] Tā’s political career was not successful, and so he completely used his family fortune to bribe the supervisor slave, with him forming marriage alliance, and over the years his family finances because of this were completely ruined. The multitude of slaves were all ashamed and asked [Mèng] Tā what he wished for. [Mèng] Tā said: “I only wish for you sirs to bow [to me].” The slaves had received his generosity for a long time, and all agreed. At the time guest retainers sought to meet [Zhāng] Ràng so that below his gates there were always several hundred carriages, some for accumulated days being unable to pass through. [Mèng] Tā at the very end arrived, the multitude of slaves watched for his arrival, all welcomed his carriage and bowed, and directly led [Mèng] Tā’s carriage alone to enter. Everyone was completely amazed, said that [Mèng] Tā was friendly with [Zhāng] Ràng, and competed to gift precious treasures to [Mèng] Tā. [Mèng] Tā obtained these and completely used them to bribe [Zhāng] Ràng. [Zhāng] Ràng was greatly pleased. [Mèng] Tā also had grape alcohol of one hú gifted to [Zhāng] Ràng, and at once was appointed Liáng Province Inspector.
[Mèng] Tā begat [Mèng] Dá, who as a youth entered Shǔ. His residence in Shǔ’s affairs and legacy are in Liú Fēng zhuàn.
Wèi lüè states: [Mèng] Dá in Yánkāng Inaugural Year led his division retainers of over four thousand families to submit to Wèi. Emperor Wén [Cáo Pī] at the time had only just succeeded the King’s throne, had already been aware of [Mèng] Dá, heard of his coming, was extremely pleased, ordered important ministers with skill in appraisal to go observe him, returning they said: “He is a talent to be an officer,” or else said: “He is a vessel to be a minister.” The King increased his admiration of [Mèng] Dá. The greeting letter to [Mèng] Dá said: “In recent days there was a command that was not enough to convey my intentions. Why? In the past Yī Zhì turned from Shāng and submitted to Zhōu, Băilǐ left Yú and entered Qín, Yuè Yì was emotionally moved by liquor purse to molt like a cicada, Wáng Zūn recognized rebellion and obedience in order to leave and arrive. All investigated the correspondences and verifications of rise and fall, understood the inevitability of success or failure, and therefore vermillion and viridian painted their appearances, good scribes recorded their achievements. Hearing that your disposition and demeanor are genuine and fine, capacity outstanding, you should employ your abilities in an enlightened time, leaving a reputation to be transmitted and recorded. Presently you completely reform yourself, cleansing scales in pure currents, extremely commendable and joyous, my open heart looking west, yearning as for an old friend, using brush to write, my joyous heart follows it. In the past Yú Qīng entered Zhào and in a second meeting became Chancellor, Chén Píng arrived at Hàn and in one audience became an advisor in the carriage. I at present have emotions for you surpassing the past, and therefore deliver my own driving horses and equipment to demonstrate loyalty and love.” It also said: “Presently Within the Seas is purified and settled, ten thousand lǐ united as one, three sides without the alarm of frontier dust, the central Xià without the apprehensions of barking dogs, and so slackens restrictions and loosens prohibitions, have no doubts with the world, the prison offices are empty and vacant, for the first time there are no hostage appointments. You are coming to join me and should understand my intentions. Carefully do not allow your family followers to cause commotions on the roads, it would be having the close disturb the distant. If you wish to come and meet me, for the time being you should first calm your division retainers, have them guaranteed secure, and only afterward slowly and gently with light riders come east.” When [Mèng] Dá arrived at Qiáo, in advancing to meet he was graceful, his talent in debate surpassed others, of the masses none did not direct their eyes. Also the King nearby set out, rode a small carriage, grasped [Mèng] Dá’s hand, patted his back, and teased him saying: “You could never be Liú Bèi’s assassin, right?” Therefore they rode together. Also applied appointment as Cavalier Regular Attendant, designate Xīnchéng Administrator, entrusted with the responsibilities of the southwest. At the time of the multitudes of ministers some believed the treatment was too much, and also inappropriate to entrust a regional responsibility. The King heard this and said: “My guarantee that there will be no other [problems] is that it is like the example of a mugwort arrow shooting into mugwort.” [Mèng] Dá had been favored by Emperor Wén and also close and friendly with Huán Jiē and Xiàhóu Shàng. When Emperor Wén passed away, at the time Huán [Jiē] and [Xiàhóu] Shàng both had died, [Mèng] Dá himself believed he was a distant traveler who had for a long time on the borders, his heart was not at ease. Zhūgě Liàng heard of this, secretly wished to entice [Mèng] Dá, repeatedly sent letters to recruit him, and [Mèng] Dá sent replies. Wèixīng Administrator Shēn Yí with [Mèng] Dá had conflict, and secretly memorialized that [Mèng] Dá was covertly communicating with Shǔ. The Emperor did not yet believe it. Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng sent Advisor to the Army Liáng Jī to investigate him, and also encourage him to enter Court. [Mèng] Dá was alarmed, and therefore rebelled.
Gān Bǎo’s Jìn jì states: When [Mèng] Dá first entered Xīnchéng, he climbed up Báimǎ fort, sighed and said: “Liú Fēng and Shēn Dān occupied metal fortresses of a thousand lǐ and yet lost this!”



〔一〕　三輔決錄曰：伯郎，涼州人，名不令休。其註曰：伯郎姓孟，名他，扶風人。靈帝時。中常侍張讓專朝政，讓監奴典護家事。他仕不遂，乃盡以家財賂監奴，與共結親，積年家業為之破盡。眾奴皆慚，問他所欲，他曰：「欲得卿曹拜耳。」奴被恩久，皆許諾。時賓客求見讓者，門下車常數百乘，或累日不得通。他最後到，眾奴伺其至，皆迎車而拜，徑將他車獨入。眾人悉驚，謂他與讓善，爭以珍物遺他。他得之，盡以賂讓，讓大喜。他又以蒲桃酒一斛遺讓，即拜涼州刺史。他生達，少入蜀。其處蜀事跡在劉封傳。魏略曰：達以延康元年率部曲四千餘家歸魏。文帝時初即王位，既宿知有達，聞其來，甚悅，令貴臣有識察者往觀之，還曰「將帥之才也」，或曰「卿相之器也」，王益欽達。逆與達書曰：「近日有命，未足達旨，何者？昔伊摯背商而歸周，百里去虞而入秦，樂毅感鴟夷以蟬蛻，王遵識逆順以去就，皆審興廢之符效，知成敗之必然，故丹青畫其形容，良史載其功勳。聞卿姿度純茂，器量優絕，當騁能明時，收名傳記。今者翻然濯鱗清流，甚相嘉樂，虛心西望，依依若舊，下筆屬辭，歡心從之。昔虞卿入趙，再見取相，陳平就漢，一覲參乘，孤今於卿，情過於往，故致所御馬物以昭忠愛。」又曰：「今者海內清定，萬里一統，三垂無邊塵之警，中夏無狗吠之虞，以是弛罔闊禁，與世無疑，保官空虛，初無（資）〔質〕任。卿來相就，當明孤意，慎勿令家人繽紛道路，以親駭疏也。若卿欲來相見，且當先安部曲，有所保固，然後徐徐輕騎來東。」達既至譙，進見閑雅，才辯過人，眾莫不屬目。又王近出，乘小輦，執達手，撫其背戲之曰：「卿得無為劉備刺客邪？」遂與同載。又加拜散騎常侍，領新城太守，委以西南之任。時眾臣或以為待之太猥，又不宜委以方任。王聞之曰：「吾保其無他，亦譬以蒿箭射蒿中耳。」達既為文帝所寵，又與桓階、夏侯尚親善，及文帝崩，時桓、尚皆卒，達自以羈旅久在疆埸，心不自安。諸葛亮聞之，陰欲誘達，數書招之，達與相報答。魏興太守申儀與達有隙，密表達與蜀潛通，帝未之信也。司馬宣王遣參軍梁幾察之，又勸其入朝。達驚懼，遂反。干寶晉紀曰：達初入新城，登白馬塞，歎曰：「劉封、申耽，據金城千里而失之乎！」







Second Year, Spring, Standard Moon [228 Feb 23 – Mar 23], [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng attacked and breached Xīnchéng, beheaded [Mèng] Dá, sent his head. [5] Divided Xīnchéng’s Shàngyōng, Wǔlíng, Wū counties to form Shàngyōng prefecture, Xī county to form Xī prefecture.



二年春正月，宣王攻破新城，斬達，傳其首。〔一〕分新城之上庸、武陵、巫縣為上庸郡，錫縣為錫郡。










[5] Wèi lüè states: [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng enticed [Mèng] Dá’s officer Lǐ Fǔ and [Mèng] Dá’s sister’s son Dèng Xián, [Dèng] Xián and others opened the gates and accepted the army. [Mèng] Dá was besieged for ten and six days and was defeated, burned his head at Luòyáng’s four road crossing.



〔一〕　魏略曰：宣王誘達將李輔及達甥鄧賢，賢等開門納軍。達被圍旬有六日而敗，焚其首于洛陽四達之衢。







Shǔ’s chief officer Zhūgě Liàng invaded the borders, Tiānshuǐ, Nán’ān, Āndìng three prefectures’ officials and civilians rebelled and welcomed [Zhūgě] Liàng. [6] Sent General-in-Chief Cáo Zhēn as Overall Commander of Guānyòu, together advancing soldiers. Right General Zhāng Hé struck [Zhūgě] Liàng at Jiētíng, greatly defeated him. [Zhūgě] Liàng was defeated and fled, the three prefectures were pacified. Dīngwèi [228 Apr 9], went to visit Cháng’ān. [7] ) Summer, Fourth Moon [228 May 22 – Jun 19] Dīngyǒu [May 29], returned to Luòyáng Palace. [8] Pardoned prisoners not condemned to death on down. Yǐsì [228 Jun 6], discussed the achievements of suppressing [Zhūgě] Liàng, enfeoffed noble ranks and increased fiefs each on distinct basis. Fifth Moon [228 Jun 20 – Jul 19], great drought. Sixth Moon [Jul 20 – Aug 17], Edict said: “Honoring classicists and valuing scholarship is the root of the King’s influence. Recently of the classicist offices some are not the appropriate men; how can one by this declare and explain the sagely ways? Thus highly select Academic Scholars with talent for appointment as Attendant Centrals and Regular Attendants. Extend the orders to the prefectures and states, that recommendation of servicemen is to use scholarship of the classics as foremost.” Autumn, Ninth Moon [228 Oct 16 – Nov 14], Cáo Xiū led the various armies to reach Wǎn, with Wú officer Lù Yì battled at Shí precinct, defeated utterly. Yǐyǒu [228 Nov 13], enthroned Imperial son [Cáo] Mù as King of Fányáng. Gēngzǐ, Marshal-in-Chief Cáo Xiū died. Winter, Tenth Moon [228 Nov 15 – Dec 13], Edict on the Excellencies and Ministers and close ministers to nominate good officers, each one man. Eleventh Moon [228 Dec 14 – 229 Jan 12], Excellency over the Masses Wáng Lǎng died. Twelfth Moon [229 Jan 13 – Feb 10], Zhūgě Liàng besieged Chéncāng, Cáo Zhēn sent General Fèi Yào and others to resist him. [9] Liáodōng Administrator Gōngsūn Gōng’s elder brother’s son [Gōngsūn] Yuān forcefully seized [Gōngsūn] Gōng’s position, therefore appointed [Gōngsūn] Yuān as designate Liáodōng Administrator.



蜀大將諸葛亮寇邊，天水、南安、安定三郡吏民叛應亮。〔一〕遣大將軍曹真都督關右，並進兵。右將軍張郃擊亮於街亭，大破之。亮敗走，三郡平。丁未，行幸長安。〔二〕夏四月丁酉，還洛陽宮。〔三〕赦繫囚非殊死以下。乙巳，論討亮功，封爵增邑各有差。五月，大旱。六月，詔曰：「尊儒貴學，王教之本也。自頃儒官或非其人，將何以宣明聖道？其高選博士，才任侍中常侍者。申敕郡國，貢士以經學為先。」秋九月，曹休率諸軍至皖，與吳將陸議戰於石亭，敗績。乙酉，立皇子穆為繁陽王。庚子，大司馬曹休薨。冬十月，詔公卿近臣舉良將各一人。十一月，司徒王朗薨。十二月，諸葛亮圍陳倉，曹真遣將軍費曜等拒之。〔四〕遼東太守公孫恭兄子淵，劫奪恭位，遂以淵領遼東太守。










[6] Wèi shū states: At the time the Court ministers did not know what plan to use. The Emperor said: “[Zhūgě] Liàng obstructed mountains for firmness. That he now personally comes accords with the military books’ techniques of delivering men. Moreover [Zhūgě] Liàng is greedy for the three prefectures, knows to advance but does not know to retreat, now at this time, defeating [Zhūgě] Liàng is certain.” Thus organized and led soldiers and horses, infantry and cavalry of fifty thousand, to resist [Zhūgě] Liàng.



〔一〕　魏書曰：是時朝臣未知計所出，帝曰：「亮阻山為固，今者自來，既合兵書致人之術；且亮貪三郡，知進而不知退，今因此時，破亮必也。」乃部勒兵馬步騎五萬拒亮。













[7] Wèi lüè records the Emperor’s spread announcement to Heaven’s Under and declaration to Yì Province stating: “Liú Bèi turned back on kindness, personally fleeing to Bā-Shǔ. Zhūgě Liàng abandons the state of his father and mother, flattering a faction of cruel bandits, divinity and humanity suffering poison, evils accumulating to bodily destruction. [Zhūgě] Liàng outside pursues a reputation for establishing an orphan, but inside covets the substance of concentrating power. Liú Shēngzhī and his brothers maintain an empty city and nothing more. [Zhūgě] Liàng also abuses and scorns Yì’s lands, oppressively exploits its people, and therefore of the Lìláng, Dàngqú Gāodìng, Qīng Qiāng, none do not collapse apart, becoming [Zhūgě] Liàng’s enemies. But yet [Zhūgě] Liàng reverses a fur coat to carry firewood, the inside worn away and the fur entirely lost, amputates toes to fit shoes, carving flesh and wounding bone, instead further bragging, believing himself capable, deploying troops at the bottom of a well, roaming and walking in the hoofprints of a cow. From since We succeeded the throne, three borders were without problems, yet I pitied that Heaven’s Under repeatedly had encountered weapons and armor, and moreover wished to nurture the elderly and aged of the Four Seas and raise the orphans and young of the later born, first shifting customs by Ritual and Music, next discussing warfare in the intervals between farming, placing [Zhūgě] Liàng beyond the planning, not yet believing him a concern. But [Zhūgě] Liàng embraces Lǐ Xióng’s ambitions of foolish valor, not considering Jīng Hán’s warning to estimate virtues, spurs and plunders officials and civilians, seeking to steal gains at Qíshān. The ruler’s brigades had just roused, [the enemy’s] courage was broken and spirit lost, Mǎ Sù and Gāo Xiáng on seeing the banners fled in defeat, the tiger ministers pursued the rout, trampling corpses and wading blood. [Zhūgě] Liàng the little fellow was shaken and afraid of Our brigades. The ferocious elite leap forth, all thinking to charge ahead. We consider that of all the lands none are not the Ruler’s subjects, ‘wherever the brigades occupy, thistles and thorns will grow,’ and do not wish to cause villages of a thousand households of the loyal and sincere and true and good to with the faction of the obscene and ignorant together receive mud and coal. Therefore I first open declarations, to make clear the state’s sincerity, encourage thoughts of change and reform, to not remain in a country of chaos. Bā-Shǔ’s officers and officials and servicemen and civilians are all forcefully coerced by [Zhūgě] Liàng, the Excellencies and Ministers on down will all be permitted to bind hands [to surrender].”



〔二〕　魏略載帝露布天下并班告益州曰：「劉備背恩，自竄巴蜀。諸葛亮棄父母之國，阿殘賊之黨，神人被毒，惡積身滅。亮外慕立孤之名，而內貪專擅之實。劉升之兄弟守空城而己。亮又侮易益土，虐用其民，是以利狼、宕渠、高定、青羌莫不瓦解，為亮仇敵。而亮反裘負薪，裏盡毛殫，刖趾適屨，刻肌傷骨，反更稱說，自以為能。行兵於井底，游步於牛蹄。自朕即位，三邊無事，猶哀憐天下數遭兵革，且欲養四海之耆老，長後生之孤幼，先移風於禮樂，次講武於農隙，置亮畫外，未以為虞。而亮懷李熊愚勇之（智）〔志〕，不思荊邯度德之戒，驅略吏民，盜利祁山。王師方振，膽破氣奪，馬謖、高祥，望旗奔敗。虎臣逐北，蹈尸涉血，亮也小子，震驚朕師。猛銳踊躍，咸思長驅。朕惟率土莫非王臣，師之所處，荊棘生焉，不欲使千室之邑忠信貞良，與夫淫昏之黨，共受塗炭。故先開示，以昭國誠，勉思變化，無滯亂邦。巴蜀將吏士民諸為亮所劫迫，公卿已下皆聽束手。」













[8] Wèi lüè states: At that time there was false rumor saying the Emperor had already passed away and the various ministers accompanying the carriage were welcoming and establishing the King of Yōngqiū [Cáo] Zhí. The capital from the Dowager Empress Biàn and the various Excellencies were all completely afraid. When the Emperor returned, all secretly examined his facial expression. The Dowager Empress Biàn was both sorrowful and happy, and wished to find the one who started the rumor. The Emperor said: “Heaven’s Under all said it, who could be found?”



〔三〕　魏略曰：是時訛言，云帝已崩，從駕群臣迎立雍丘王植。京師自卞太后群公盡懼。及帝還，皆私察顏色。卞太后悲喜，欲推始言者，帝曰：「天下皆言，將何所推？」













[9] Wèi lüè states: Before this, sent General Hǎo Zhāo to build Chéncāng city walls. It happened that [Zhūgě] Liàng arrived, besieged [Hǎo] Zhāo, could not capture it. [Hǎo] Zhāo appellation Bódào was a Tàiyuán man, as a man heroic and strong, as a youth entered the army and became a division retainer commander, repeatedly had battle achievements, became a miscellaneous title General, and so defended the Hé’s west for over ten years, the civilians and Yí feared and submitted to him. [Zhūgě] Liàng besieged Chéncāng and sent [Hǎo] Zhāo’s fellow townsman Jìn Xiáng to the outside of the city walls to from afar persuade him. [Hǎo] Zhāo from atop a tower answered [Jìn] Xiáng saying: “The Wèi House’s laws, you are familiar with. My conduct as a man, you understand. My receiving of the state’s favor is much and my household is valued, there is nothing that you can say, there is only certain death. You return and apologize to Zhūgě, and then he can attack.” [Jìn] Xiáng informed [Zhūgě] Liàng of [Hǎo] Zhāo’s speech. [Zhūgě] Liàng again sent [Jìn] Xiáng to again persuade [Hǎo] Zhāo, saying that their soldiers were no match and there was no reason to bring about their own extermination in vain. [Hǎo] Zhāo spoke to [Jìn Xiáng] stating: “My previous words are already settled. I may recognize you, but arrows do not recognize you.” [Jìn] Xiáng thus left. [Zhūgě] Liàng himself believed that he had multitudes of several tens of thousands while [Hǎo] Zhāo’s soldiers were only over a thousand men, and also estimated that eastern rescue would not be able to quickly arrive, and so advanced soldiers to attack [Hǎo] Zhāo, raising scaling ladders and charging carts to overlook the city walls. [Hǎo] Zhāo thereupon used fire arrows to oppose and shoot the scaling ladders, the ladders burned, and the men atop the ladders all burned to death. [Hǎo] Zhāo also used rope linked grindstones to crush the charging carts, the charging carts were broken. [Zhūgě] Liàng thus again made lattice railings of a hundred chǐ to shoot into the city walls, used dirt balls to fill in the moat, wishing to directly climb the city walls, [Hǎo] Zhāo also inside built another layer of walls. [Zhūgě] Liàng also made earthen tunnels, wishing to leap out into the city interior, [Hǎo] Zhāo also within the city walls dug the ground horizontally to intercept them. Day and night, they attacked and resisted one another for over twenty days, [Zhūgě] Liàng was without plans, rescue arrived, [Zhūgě Liàng] withdrew and retreated. Edict commended [Hǎo] Zhāo’s excellent defense, bestowed noble title as a Ranked Marquess. When he returned, the Emperor invited him to an audience and showed appreciation for his labors, looking back to say to Central Writers Director Sūn Zī stating: “Your hometown then had you as a great minister, and a General as glorious as this. We will have what further worries?” Further wished to greatly employ him, it happened he fell ill and died, his Legacy Order warned his son [Hǎo] Kǎi saying: “I was a General and know that a General is not something to be. I repeatedly excavated graves, taking their wood to make war equipment, and also know that lavish burial is of no benefit to the dead. You must dress in seasonal clothes. Moreover, a man only has a place while living; where are the dead? Now we are far away from our ancestral graves, east or west or south or north, [my burial place] is up to you and nothing more.”



〔四〕　魏略曰：先是，使將軍郝昭築陳倉城；會亮至，圍昭，不能拔。昭字伯道，太原人，為人雄壯，少入軍為部曲督，數有戰功，為雜號將軍，遂鎮守河西十餘年，民夷畏服。亮圍陳倉，使昭鄉人靳詳於城外遙說之，昭於樓上應詳曰：「魏家科法，卿所練也；我之為人，卿所知也。我受國恩多而門戶重，卿無可言者，但有必死耳。卿還謝諸葛，便可攻也。」詳以昭語告亮，亮又使詳重說昭，言人兵不敵，無為空自破滅。昭謂詳曰：「前言已定矣。我識卿耳，箭不識也。」詳乃去。亮自以有眾數萬，而昭兵纔千餘人，又度東救未能便到，乃進兵攻昭，起雲梯衝車以臨城。昭於是以火箭逆射其雲梯，梯然，梯上人皆燒死。昭又以繩連石磨壓其衝車，衝車折。亮乃更為井闌百尺以射城中，以土丸填塹，欲直攀城，昭又於內築重牆。亮又為地突，欲踊出於城裏，昭又於城內穿地橫截之。晝夜相攻拒二十餘日，亮無計，救至，引退。詔嘉昭善守，賜爵列侯。及還，帝引見慰勞之，顧謂中書令孫資曰：「卿鄉里乃有爾曹快人，為將灼如此，朕復何憂乎？」仍欲大用之。會病亡，遺令戒其子凱曰：「吾為將，知將不可為也。吾數發塚，取其木以為攻戰具，又知厚葬無益於死者也。汝必斂以時服。且人生有處所耳，死復何在耶？今去本墓遠，東西南北，在汝而已。」







Third Year, Summer, Fourth Moon [229 May 11 – Jun 9], the King of Yuánchéng [Cáo] Lǐ died. Sixth Moon [229 Jul 9 – Aug 7] Guǐmǎo [229 Jul 29], the King of Fányáng [Cáo] Mù died. Wùshēn [229 Aug 3], posthumously honored his great-great-grandfather the Chief Prolonging Autumn [Cáo Téng] as Gāo Huángdì, and [Cáo Téng’s] consort Wú-shì as Gāo Huánghòu.



三年夏四月，元城王禮薨。六月癸卯，繁陽王穆薨。戊申，追尊高祖大長秋曰高皇帝，夫人吳氏曰高皇后。




Autumn, Seventh Moon [229 Aug 8 – Sep 5], Edict said: “By Ritual, when the ruler is without successor, select and establish a branch son to continue the main clan. Then he will continue the standard succession and serve public righteousness; how can he again look back to his private parents? Hàn Xuān continued as Emperor Zhāo’s posterity but applied on his deceased father Dào a title as an Imperial; Emperor Āi as an outer vassal was enthroned, but Dǒng Hóng and the rest praised and cited fallen Qín to confuse and mislead that time’s Court, so that they honored Imperial Gōng and established a temple in the capital city, and also favored the vassal concubine [Emperor Āi’s birth mother], having her comparable to Chángxìn [Dowager Empress], rearranging the Zhāo-Mù in the Front Hall, altogether four positions in the East Palace, the presumptuousness and inappropriateness without limit, Humanity and Divinity would not bless it, and yet they blamed and punished the loyal and upright remonstration of Shī Dān, and so incurred the calamities of the burnings of Dīng and Fù. From then on afterward, it was followed and enacted continuously. In the past when Lǔ Wén violated sacrifices, the crime was by Xiàfù; when Sòng state transgressed limits, the ridicule was on Huà Yuán. Thus order the Excellencies and Ministers and relevant managers to deeply take the conduct and affairs of former eras as warning. If ten thousand to one a later successor should come from the vassal lords entering to serve the main line, then he must clearly understand the meanings of becoming a man’s posterity. If anyone dares be a flattering and corrupting influence, guiding and cajoling the time’s lord, to presumptuously establish incorrect titles to violate the correct succession line, calling deceased father as Imperial, declaring deceased mother as Empress, then the leg and arm great ministers are to execute them without pardon. Thus write this on metal tablets, store this in the Ancestral Temple, make known as law canon.”



秋七月，詔曰：「禮，王后無嗣，擇建支子以繼大宗，則當纂正統而奉公義，何得復顧私親哉！漢宣繼昭帝後，加悼考以皇號；哀帝以外藩援立，而董宏等稱引亡秦，惑誤時朝，既尊恭皇，立廟京都，又寵藩妾，使比長信，敘昭穆於前殿，並四位於東宮，僭差無度，人神弗祐，而非罪師丹忠正之諫，用致丁、傅焚如之禍。自是之後，相踵行之。昔魯文逆祀，罪由夏父；宋國非度，譏在華元。其令公卿有司，深以前世行事為戒。後嗣萬一有由諸侯入奉大統，則當明為人後之義；敢為佞邪導諛時君，妄建非正之號以干正統，謂考為皇，稱妣為后，則股肱大臣，誅之無赦。其書之金策，藏之宗廟，著於令典。」




Winter, Tenth Moon [229 Nov 4 – Dec 3], changed Píngwàng watchtower to Tīngsòng watchtower. The Emperor always said: “Litigation is the arbiter of the lives of Heaven’s Under.” Every time deciding a great lawsuit, he always visited the watchtower to oversee and hear it.



冬十月，改平望觀曰聽訟觀。帝常言「獄者，天下之性命也」，每斷大獄，常幸觀臨聽之。




Previously, Luòyáng’s Ancestral Temple was not yet complete, the Spirit Tablets were at Yè’s Temple. Eleventh Moon [229 Dec 4 – 230 Jan 1], the Temple was first completed, sent Minister of Ceremonies Hán Jì Holding Stave to welcome the Spirit Tablets of Gāo Huángdì, Tài Huángdì, Wǔ-dì, Wén-dì from Yè. Twelfth Moon [230 Jan 2 – Jan 31], Jǐchǒu [230 Jan 11], arrived, accepted and secured the Spirit Tablets in the Temple. [10]



初，洛陽宗廟未成，神主在鄴廟。十一月，廟始成，使太常韓暨持節迎高皇帝、太皇帝、武帝、文帝神主于鄴，十二月己丑至，奉安神主于廟。〔一〕










[10] Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: Huángchū Fourth Year [223], relevant managers memorialized to establish two temples, with Tài Huángdì [Cáo Sōng], the Chief Prolonging Autumn [Cáo Téng], and Wén-dì’s great-great-grandfather [Cáo Mēng] together as one temple, and specially establish Wǔ-dì’s temple to for a hundred generations not be demolished. Now here there is no great-great-grandfather Spirit Tablet, probably as the degree of relation was exhausted and it was demolished. This then is that at Wèi’s beginning they only established a family temple, sacrificing in four rooms and nothing more. Reaching to Jǐngchū Inaugural Year, they first set the Seven Temples system.
Sūn Shèng states: Serve the deceased as if they remain, sacrifice as if the spirits are there. Welcoming and moving the Spirit Tablets was correct in its appropriateness.



〔一〕　臣松之按：黃初四年，有司奏立二廟，太皇帝大長秋與文帝之高祖共一廟，特立武帝廟，百世不毀。今此無高祖神主，蓋以親盡毀也。此則魏初唯立親廟，祀四室而已。至景初元年，始定七廟之制。孫盛曰：事亡猶存，祭如神在，迎遷神主，正斯宜矣。







Guǐmǎo [230 Jan 25], the Dà Yuèzhī King Bō Diào sent envoy to present tribute, appointed [Bō] Diào as Qīn Wèi Dà Yuèzhī King.



癸卯，大月氏王波調遣使奉獻，以調為親魏大月氏王。




Fourth Year, Spring, Second Moon [230 Mar 2 – Mar 31], Rénwǔ [230 Mar 5], Edict said: “Whether the world is simple or refined, by teachings then it changes. Since the chaos of war onward, scholarship of the classics was abandoned and cut off, the later born in seeking advancement do not follow canonical practices. Is it that instruction and guidance are not extensive, that the ones about to be advanced and employed are not made prominent for their virtue? Thus for cadets and clerks that have studied through a classic and have capability for appointment to govern the people, academic scholars are to hold examinations and promote the highest ranked for urgent employment. Thus those pretentious and flowery that do not attend to morals and fundamentals are all to be dismissed and removed.” Wùzǐ [230 Mar 11], Edict on the Grand Tutor and Three Excellencies to have Emperor Wén’s Diǎnlùn carved on stone and set outside the Temple Gates. Guǐsì [230 Mar 16], appointed General-in-Chief Cáo Zhēn as Marshal-in-Chief, Agile Cavalry General Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng as General-in-Chief, Liáodōng Administrator Gōngsūn Yuān as Chariots and Cavalry General. Summer, Fourth Moon [230 Apr 30 – May 29], Grand Tutor Zhōng Yáo died. Sixth Moon [230 Jun 29 – Jul 27], Wùzǐ [230 Jul 9], the Grand Imperial Dowager Empress passed away. Bǐngshēn [230 Jul 17], abolished Shàngyōng prefecture. Autumn, Seventh Moon [230 Jul 28 – Aug 26], Wǔ-Xuān Empress Biàn was entombed and buried at Gāolìng. Edict on Marshal-in-Chief Cáo Zhēn and General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng to attack Shǔ. Eighth Moon [230 Aug 27 – Sep 24], Xīnsì [230 Aug 31], went on eastern tour, sent envoy to with one bull ox sacrifice at the Center Peak. [11] Yǐwèi [230 Sep 14], visited Xǔchāng Palace. Ninth Moon [230 Sep 25 – Oct 24], heavy rain, the Yī, Luò, Hé, and Hàn rivers overflowed, Edict on [Cáo] Zhēn and the rest to withdraw the brigades. Winter, Tenth Moon [230 Nov 23 – Dec 22], Yǐmǎo [230 Dec 3], went back to Luòyáng Palace. Gēngshēn [230 Dec 8], Ordered: “Crimes that are not death sentences are to consider ransoms, each on distinct basis.” Eleventh Moon [230 Dec 23 – 231 Jan 20], Tàibái crossed Suìxīng. Twelfth Moon [231 Jan 21 – Feb 19], Xīnwèi [231 Feb 17], changed the burial of Wén-Zhāo Empress Zhēn to Cháoyánglíng. Bǐngyín [231 Feb 12], Edict on the Excellencies and Ministers to nominate Worthy-Good [candidates].



四年春二月壬午，詔曰：「世之質文，隨教而變。兵亂以來，經學廢絕，後生進趣，不由典謨。豈訓導未洽，將進用者不以德顯乎？其郎吏學通一經，才任牧民，博士課試，擢其高第者，亟用；其浮華不務道本者，皆罷退之。」戊子，詔太傅三公：以文帝典論刻石，立于廟門之外。癸巳，以大將軍曹真為大司馬，驃騎將軍司馬宣王為大將軍，遼東太守公孫淵為車騎將軍。夏四月，太傅鍾繇薨。六月戊子，太皇太后崩。丙申，省上庸郡。秋七月，武宣卞后祔葬于高陵。詔大司馬曹真、大將軍司馬宣王伐蜀。八月辛巳，行東巡，遣使者以特牛祠中嶽。〔一〕乙未，幸許昌宮。九月，大雨，伊、洛、河、漢水溢，詔真等班師。冬十月乙卯，行還洛陽宮。庚申，令：「罪非殊死聽贖各有差。」十一月，太白犯歲星。十二月辛未，改葬文昭甄后于朝陽陵。丙寅，詔公卿舉賢良。










[11] Wèi shū states: Went past Fánchāng, sent Metal Mace Bearer Zāng Bà to Enact Grand Commandant affairs, to with one bull ox sacrifice to the platform of receiving the abdication. Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: Hàn jì, Emperor Zhāng’s Yuánhé Third Year [86], Edict on Gāoyì county to sacrifice at the platform of ascending the throne at Wǔchéngmò comparable to the Là sacrifices of the gate doors. Although this was the previous dynasty’s already enacted precedent, however the purpose of a platform is for sacrifices to Heaven, but a platform is not a divinity. Now for there to be no services to Highest God and to yet convey offerings to an empty platform, searching the ceremony canons, it is uncertain what it was in accordance to.



〔一〕　魏書曰：行過繁昌，使執金吾臧霸行太尉事，以特牛祠受禪壇。臣松之按：漢紀章帝元和三年，詔高邑縣祠即位壇，五成陌，比臘祠門戶。此雖前代已行故事，然為壇以祀天，而壇非神也，今無事於上帝，而致祀於虛壇，求之義典，未詳所據。







Fifth Year, Spring, Standard Moon [231 Feb 20 – Mar 20], the Emperor plowed the Register Field. Third Moon, [231 Apr 20 – May 18], Marshal-in-Chief Cáo Zhēn died. Zhūgě Liàng invaded Tiānshuǐ, Edict on General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng to resist him. From the previous winter Tenth Moon reaching to This Moon there was no rain. Xīnsì [231 Apr 28], Great Sacrifices for Rain. Summer, Fourth Moon [231 May 19 – Jun 17], the Xiānbēi Adhering to Righteousness King Kē Bǐnéng led his tribesmen with the Dīnglíng Chieftain Érchán to visit Yōu Province to tribute famed horses. Restored the installation of a Protector of the Xiōngnú Central Cadet General. Autumn, Seventh Moon [231 Aug 16 – Sep 13], Bǐngzǐ [231 Aug 21], as [Zhūgě] Liàng had retreated and fled, enfeoffed noble titles and increased ranks each on distinct basis. [12] Yǐyǒu [231 Aug 30], Imperial son [Cáo] Yīn was born, Great Amnesty.



五年春正月，帝耕于籍田。三月，大司馬曹真薨。諸葛亮寇天水，詔大將軍司馬宣王拒之。自去冬十月至此月不雨，辛巳，大雩。夏四月，鮮卑附義王軻比能率其種人及丁零大人兒禪詣幽州貢名馬。復置護匈奴中郎將。秋七月丙子，以亮退走，封爵增位各有差。〔一〕乙酉，皇子殷生，大赦。










[12] Wèi shū states: Previously, when [Zhūgě] Liàng set out, commentators believed that as [Zhūgě] Liàng’s army was without a supply train, provisions certainly could not be connected, without striking them they would be defeated on their own, and there was no reason to labor the soldiers. Some wished to themselves cut down Shàngguī’s left and right growing wheat to deny the rebels of food. The Emperor completely did not listen. Beginning to end sent soldiers to increase [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s army, and also ordered to have them protect the wheat. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng with [Zhūgě] Liàng were locked together, depending on this wheat for army provisions.



〔一〕　魏書曰：初，亮出，議者以為亮軍無輜重，糧必不繼，不擊自破，無為勞兵；或欲自芟上邽左右生麥以奪賊食，帝皆不從。前後遣兵增宣王軍，又敕使護麥。宣王與亮相持，賴得此麥以為軍糧。







Eighth Moon [231 Sep 14 – Oct 13], Edict said: “In antiquity, the vassal lords visited Court in order to promote friendships and closeness, to harmonize the myriad states. That the Former Emperor wrote Order not wishing to allow the various kings to be in the capital, was to say that a young Ruler was on the throne and the mother dowager controlling the government, guarding against the slightest for the gradual effects, concerned with overall flourishing and decline. When We ponder having not met with the various kings for ten and two years, feelings of distant longing, can they not appear in thought? Thus order the various kings and the Imperial Clan dukes and marquesses to each bring a legitimate son of one man to Court. Later if there is a young Ruler and a mother dowager in the Palace, it will be as the Former Emperor’s Order, clearly written in law.” Winter, Eleventh Moon [231 Dec 12 – 232 Jan 10], Yǐyǒu [231 Dec 28], the Moon crossed Xuānyuán large star. Wùxū [232 Jan 10], last day of the moon, the sun was eclipsed. Twelfth Moon [232 Jan 11 – Feb 8], Jiǎchén [232 Jan 16], the Moon crossed Zhènxīng. Wùwǔ [232 Jan 30], Grand Commandant Huà Xīn died.



八月，詔曰：「古者諸侯朝聘，所以敦睦親親協和萬國也。先帝著令，不欲使諸王在京都者，謂幼主在位，母后攝政，防微以漸，關諸盛衰也。朕惟不見諸王十有二載，悠悠之懷，能不興思！其令諸王及宗室公侯各將適子一人朝。後有少主、母后在宮者，自如先帝令，申明著于令。」冬十一月乙酉，月犯軒轅大星。戊戌晦，日有蝕之。十二月甲辰，月犯鎮星。戊午，太尉華歆薨。




Sixth Year, Spring, Second Moon [232 Mar 10 – Apr 7], Edict said: “The Emperors and Kings of antiquity enfeoffed and established vassal lords in order to have fence screens for the ruling house. Does the Shī not say: ‘Embracing virtue maintains peace, clan sons maintain walls.’ Qín and Hàn succeeded Zhōu, sometimes too strong sometimes too weak, always missing the balance. Great Wèi begins its enterprise, the various kings’ founding states followed what was appropriate for the time, not yet having a definite system. This is not the way to propagate laws for posterity. Thus change the enfeoffments of the vassal lord kings, all to have prefectures as states.” Third Moon [232 Apr 8 – May 7], Guǐyǒu [232 Apr 14], went on eastern tour, wherever he passed he stopped to ask after the highly aged and the widowers and widows and orphans and childless, bestowing grain and silk. Yǐhài [232 Apr 16], the Moon crossed Xuānyuán large star. Summer, Fourth Moon [232 May 8 – Jun 5], Rényín [232 May 13], went to visit Xǔchāng Palace. Jiǎzǐ [232 Jun 4], first advanced fresh fruit in the Temple. Fifth Moon [232 Jun 6 – Jul 5], Imperial son [Cáo] Yīn died, posthumously enfeoffed with posthumous name King Āi of Ānpíng. Autumn, Seventh Moon [232 Aug 4 – Sep 2], appointed Minister of the Guard Dǒng Zhāo as Excellency over the Masses. Ninth Moon [232 Oct 2 – Oct 31], went to visit Móbēi, built Xǔchāng Palace, raised Jǐngfú and Chéngguāng Halls. Winter, Tenth Moon [232 Nov 1 – Nov 29], Exterminating Yí General Tián Yù commanded multitudes to suppress Wú officer Zhōu Hè at Chéngshān, killing [Zhōu] Hé. Eleventh Moon [232 Nov 30 – Dec 29], Bǐngyín [232 Dec 3], Tàibái in daytime seen. There was a comet in Yì, near Tàiwēi’s Shàngjiàng stars. Gēngyín [232 Dec 27], King Sī of Chén [Cáo] Zhí died. Twelfth Moon [232 Dec 30 – 233 Jan 27], went back to Xǔchāng Palace.



六年春二月，詔曰：「古之帝王，封建諸侯，所以藩屏王室也。詩不云乎，『懷德維寧，宗子維城』。秦、漢繼周，或彊或弱，俱失厥中。大魏創業，諸王開國，隨時之宜，未有定制，非所以永為後法也。其改封諸侯王，皆以郡為國。」三月癸酉，行東巡，所過存問高年鰥寡孤獨，賜穀帛。乙亥，月犯軒轅大星。夏四月壬寅，行幸許昌宮。甲子，初進新果于廟。五月，皇子殷薨，追封諡安平哀王。秋七月，以衛尉董昭為司徒。九月，行幸摩陂，治許昌宮，起景福、承光殿。冬十月，殄夷將軍田豫帥眾討吳將周賀於成山，殺賀。十一月丙寅，太白晝見。有星孛于翼，近太微上將星。庚寅，陳思王植薨。十二月，行還許昌宮。

title: 3  Annals of Emperor Míng
text:
Qīnglóng (233 - 236)


Qīnglóng Inaugural Year, Spring, Standard Moon [233 Jan 28 – Feb 26], Jiǎshēn [233 Feb 19], green dragon sighted at Jiá’s Móbēi inside a well. Second Moon [233 Feb 27 – Mar 28], Dīngyǒu [233 Mar 4], visited Móbēi to observe the dragon, thereupon changed the Year, changed Móbēi to Lóngbēi, bestowed on adult males noble rank of level two, widowers and widows and orphans and childless were not to pay this year’s taxes. Third Moon [233 Mar 29 – Apr 26], Jiǎzǐ [233 Mar 31], Edict on the Excellencies and Ministers to nominate servicemen, Worthy-Good and Sincere-Conduct, each one man. Summer, Fifth Moon [233 May 27 – Jun 24], Rénshēn [233 Jun 7], Edict to sacrifice to former General-in-Chief Xiàhóu Dūn, Marshal-in-Chief Cáo Rén, Chariots and Cavalry General Chéng Yù in Tàizǔ Temple Hall. [13] Wùyín [233 Jun 13], the King of Běihǎi [Cáo] Ruí died. Intercalary Moon [233 Jun 25 – Jul 24], Gēngyín [233 Jun 25], first day of the moon, the sun was eclipsed. Dīngyǒu [233 Jun 2], changed the enfeoffments of Imperial Clan daughters that were not the daughters of the various kings to all be princesses of towns. Edict on the various prefectures and states that mountains and rivers not in sacrificial canon were not to receive sacrifices. Sixth Moon [233 Jul 25 – Aug 22], Luòyáng Palace’s Jūshì burned down.



青龍元年春正月甲申，青龍見郟之摩陂井中。二月丁酉，幸摩陂觀龍，於是改年；改摩陂為龍陂，賜男子爵人二級，鰥寡孤獨無出今年租賦。三月甲子，詔公卿舉賢良篤行之士各一人。夏五月壬申，詔祀故大將軍夏侯惇、大司馬曹仁、車騎將軍程昱於太祖廟庭。〔一〕戊寅，北海王蕤薨。閏月庚寅朔，日有蝕之。丁酉，改封宗室女非諸王女皆為邑主。詔諸郡國山川不在祠典者勿祠。六月，洛陽宮鞠室災。










[13] Wèi shū states records the Edict stating: “In the past in the rituals of the former kings, to the meritorious ministers when alive then make prominent their noble rank and salary, when gone then sacrifice to them at Dà Zhēng, therefore the Hàn clan’s meritorious ministers received sacrifices in the Temple Hall. The ministers of Great Wèi’s inaugural achievement have accomplishments and merits excellent and proven, end and beginning glorious and brilliant, thus all in compliance to ritual sacrifice to them.” Thereupon [Xiàhóu] Dūn and the rest received accompanying offerings.



〔一〕　魏書載詔曰：「昔先王之禮，於功臣存則顯其爵祿，沒則祭於大蒸，故漢氏功臣，祀於廟庭。大魏元功之臣功勳優著，終始休明者，其皆依禮祀之。」於是以惇等配饗。







Protecting the Border Passes Xiānbēi Chieftain Bùdùgēn with the rebelling Xiānbēi Chieftain Kē Bǐnéng secretly communicated, Bìng Province Inspector Bì Guǐ memorialized to at once sent out the army to outside intimidate [Kē] Bǐnéng and inside subdue Bùdùgēn. The Emperor reviewed the memorial and said: “Bùdùgēn believes he is being enticed by [Kē] Bǐnéng and has a heart doubtful of his own situation. Now if [Bì] Guǐ sends out the army, it will only cause the two divisions to be alarmed and combine into one. What intimidation and subduing would there be?” Urgently ordered [Bì] Guǐ in sending out the army to be careful not to cross the border passes past Jùzhù. By the time the Edict letter arrived, [Bì] Guǐ had advanced the army to garrison Yīnguǎn, sent Generals Sū Shàng and Dǒng Bì to pursue the Xiānbēi. [Kē] Bǐnéng had sent his son to lead over a thousand cavalry to welcome Bùdùgēn’s tribe, with [Sū] Shàng and [Dǒng] Bì encountered one another, battled at Lóufán, the two Generals were lost. Bùdùgēn’s tribe all rebelled and went out the border passes, with [Kē] Bǐnéng combining to raid the borders. Sent Valiant Cavalry General Qín Lǎng to lead the Central Army to suppress them, the caitiffs thus fled north of the desert.



保塞鮮卑大人步度根與叛鮮卑大人軻比能私通，并州刺史畢軌表，輒出軍以外威比能，內鎮步度根。帝省表曰：「步度根以為比能所誘，有自疑心。今軌出軍，適使二部驚合為一，何所威鎮乎？」促敕軌，以出軍者慎勿越塞過句注也。比詔書到，軌以進軍屯陰館，遣將軍蘇尚、董弼追鮮卑。比能遣子將千餘騎迎步度根部落，與尚、弼相遇，戰於樓煩，二將〔敗〕沒。步度根部落皆叛出塞，與比能合寇邊。遣驍騎將軍秦朗將中軍討之，虜乃走漠北。




Autumn, Ninth Moon [233 Oct 21 – Nov 19], Āndìng’s Protecting the Border Passes Xiōngnú Chieftain Húbójūzīzhí and others rebelled, Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng sent General Hú Zūn and others to pursue and suppress, defeated and forced their surrender.



秋九月，安定保塞匈奴大人胡薄居姿職等叛，司馬宣王遣將軍胡遵等追討，破降之。




Winter, Tenth Moon [233 Nov 11 – Dec 18], Bùdùgēn’s tribe’s Chieftain Dàihú’ēlángní and others visited Bìng Province to surrender. [Qín] Lǎng led the army to return. [14]



冬十月，步度根部落大人戴胡阿狼泥等詣并州降，朗引軍還〔一〕。










[14] Wèishì Chūnqiū states: [Qín] Lǎng appellation Yuánmíng was a Xīnxīng man.
Xiàn-dì zhuàn states: [Qín] Lǎng’s father named [Qín] Yílù was sent by Lǚ Bù to visit Yuán Shù, [Yuán] Shù had him take as wife a Hàn Imperial Clan daughter. His former wife Dù-shì remained at Xiàpī. When [Lǚ] Bù was being besieged, Guān Yǔ repeatedly sent requests to Tàizǔ [Cáo Cāo] to take Dù-shì as a wife. Tàizǔ suspected she had beauty, and when the city fell, Tàizǔ met her, and so himself accepted her. [Qín] Yílù returned to surrender, and was appointed Zhì Chief. When Liú Bèi fled Xiǎopèi, Zhāng Fēi accompanied him, passed by and spoke to [Qín] Yílù saying: “A man took your wife, but yet you serve him as a [county] Chief. Why be an ignorant worm like this? Why not accompany us and leave?” [Qín] Yílù followed him for several lǐ, regretted and wished to return, [Zhāng] Fēi killed him. [Qín] Lǎng accompanied his mother and was raised in the Duke’s Palace. Tàizǔ extremely loved him, every time seated in attendance he said to his guest retainers: “Does the world have anyone who loves their stepson like me?”
Wèi lüè states: [Qín] Lǎng roamed among the vassal lords, and through the reigns of Wǔ [Cáo Cāo] and Wén [Cáo Pī] was yet without faults. Reaching to Emperor Míng succeeding the throne, he was conferred with an inner office, became Valiant Cavalry General, Dispensing Affairs Central. Every time the Chariot Carriage went out or in, [Qín] Lǎng always accompanied. At the time Emperor Míng enjoyed raising [legal] citations, repeatedly there were light and trivial cases that were yet delivered to capital punishment. [Qín] Lǎng to the end did not remonstrate to stop, and also never once nominated one good person. The Emperor also because of their close affection always consulted him, often calling him by his childhood appellation Ā’Sū, repeatedly applied rewards and bestowments, raised a large mansion for him within the capital walls. Although the Four Quarters knew [Qín] Lǎng was without ability to add benefit, but yet because he was closely attached to the Utmost Honored, often gave him bribes and gifts, his wealth equal to the Dukes and Marquesses.
Shìyǔ states: [Qín] Lǎng’s son [Qín] Xiù was stern and strict and able to speak bluntly, and for Jìn Emperor Wǔ became an Academic Scholar.
Wèi lüè has [Qín] Lǎng with Kǒng Guì together in the Flatterer Intimates chapter. [Kǒng] Guì appellation Shūlín was a Tiānshuǐ man. At Jiàn’ān’s beginning, he was repeatedly sent by General Yáng Qiū to visit Tàizǔ, Tàizǔ memorialized to appoint him a Cavalry Commandant. [Kǒng] Guì by nature pandered, excelled in board games and kicking balls, therefore Tàizǔ favored him, always having him among his Left and Right, accompanying and following in going out and in. [Kǒng] Guì observed Tàizǔ’s moods, and at times when he was pleased and happy, took advantage to speak melodiously of his proposals, and in affairs many were followed, repeatedly obtaining rewards and bestowals. Many people offered gifts, [Kǒng] Guì because of this dressed as a marquess and ate with jade [utensils]. Tàizǔ favored [Kǒng] Guì, and the Five Offices General [Cáo Pī] with the vassal lords also all were close with him. From then afterward [Kǒng] Guì observed that Tàizǔ for a long time had not established an Heir-Apparent and yet had intentions on the Marquess of Línzī [Cáo Zhí], and therefore further closely attached to the Marquess of Línzī and neglected the Five Offices General, and the General extremely resented this. When Tàizǔ died, Emperor Wén succeeded the King’s throne, but had not yet delivered a punishment. Huángchū Inaugural Year [220], in following routine transfer appointed as Attached Horse Commandant. But [Kǒng] Guì secretly accepted Western Regions goods as bribes, agreeing to act on behalf of others. The matter was discovered, there was Edict to arrest and investigate, and therefore killed him.
Yú Huàn states: When those above do not confer for no reason and those below do not receive for no reason, only afterward is the exterior without the sighs of Fátán, the interior without the criticism of sinecures, the beauty of the harmonious abundance proven, the law of Grand Peace manifest. But the sorts as the flatterer intimates only pander to the ruler of men, to the point that those without virtue yet are honored, those without achievement yet receive salary. If it is so, how will it not cause the correct and upright to be daily reduced, the deviant and evil to increase all the more? With Wǔ Huángdì’s caution in rewards and Míng Huángdì’s maintaining law, yet there were still those like these men, so yet all the more for those below them!



〔一〕　魏氏春秋曰：朗字元明，新興人。獻帝傳曰：朗父名宜祿，為呂布使詣袁術，術妻以漢宗室女。其前妻杜氏留下邳。布之被圍，關羽屢請於太祖，求以杜氏為妻，太祖疑其有色，及城陷，太祖見之，乃自納之。宜祿歸降，以為銍長。及劉備走小沛，張飛隨之，過謂宜祿曰：「人取汝妻，而為之長，乃蚩蚩若是邪！隨我去乎？」宜祿從之數里，悔欲還，飛殺之。朗隨母氏畜于公宮，太祖甚愛之，每坐席，謂賓客曰：「世有人愛假子如孤者乎？」魏略曰：朗游遨諸侯間，歷武、文之世而無尤也。及明帝即位，授以內官，為驍騎將軍、給事中，每車駕出入，朗常隨從。時明帝喜發舉，數有以輕微而致大辟者，朗終不能有所諫止，又未嘗進一善人，帝亦以是親愛；每顧問之，多呼其小字阿穌，數加賞賜，為起大第於京城中。四方雖知朗無能為益，猶以附近至尊，多賂遺之，富均公侯。世語曰：朗子秀，勁厲能直言，為晉武帝博士。魏略以朗與孔桂俱在佞倖篇。桂字叔林，天水人也。建安初，數為將軍楊秋使詣太祖，太祖表拜騎都尉。桂性便辟，曉博弈、蹹鞠，故太祖愛之，每在左右，出入隨從。桂察太祖意，喜樂之時，因言次曲有所陳，事多見從，數得賞賜，人多餽遺，桂由此侯服玉食。太祖既愛桂，五官將及諸侯亦皆親之。其後桂見太祖久不立太子，而有意於臨菑侯，因更親附臨菑侯而簡於五官將，將甚銜之。及太祖薨，文帝即王位，未及致其罪。黃初元年，隨例轉拜駙馬都尉。而桂私受西域貨賂，許為人事。事發，有詔收問，遂殺之。魚豢曰：為上者不虛授，處下者不虛受，然後外無伐檀之歎，內無尸素之刺，雍熙之美著，太平之律顯矣。而佞倖之徒，但姑息人主，至乃無德而榮，無功而祿，如是焉得不使中正日朘，傾邪滋多乎！以武皇帝之慎賞，明皇帝之持法，而猶有若此等人，而況下斯者乎？







Twelfth Moon [234 Jan 18 – Feb 15], Gōngsūn Yuān beheaded and sent the heads of Sūn Quán’s dispatched envoys Zhāng Mí and Xǔ Yàn, appointed [Gōngsūn] Yuān as Marshal-in-Chief and Duke of Lèláng. [15]



十二月，公孫淵斬送孫權所遣使張彌、許晏首，以淵為大司馬樂浪公。〔一〕










[15] Shìyǔ states: Bìng Province Inspector Bì Guǐ sent Hàn’s former Crossing the Liáo General Fàn Míngyǒu’s Xiānbēi slave, aged three hundred fifty years, who spoke and drank and ate like an ordinary person. The slave said: “Huò Xiǎn was [Huò] Guāng’s later lesser wife. [Fàn] Míngyǒu’s wife was [Huò] Guāng’s previous wife’s daughter.”
Bówùzhì states: At the time in the capital city there was one person, his family and personal name lost, who ate as much as ten and some people, and therefore was fat and unable to move. His father once had been a chief clerk in a distant region, the government relocated and sent him to that county, ordering the public hostels to provide for and feed him, Within one to two years, an entire village because of this became impoverished.
Fù-zǐ states: At the time Tàiyuán excavated a burial mound and broke open a coffin, inside the coffin was a living woman. Brought out and spoken to, she was a living person. She was sent to the capital, asked about her origins, and she did not know. Inspecting the trees above the burial mound they could be thirty years old. It is unknown if this woman for thirty years was alive inside the ground, or if one morning she suddenly appeared just to meet the burial mound excavators.



〔一〕　世語曰：并州刺史畢軌送漢故度遼將軍范明友鮮卑奴，年三百五十歲，言語飲食如常人。奴云：「霍顯，光後小妻。明友妻，光前妻女。」博物志曰：時京邑有一人，失其姓名，食啖兼十許人，遂肥不能動。其父曾作遠方長吏，官徙送彼縣，令故義傳供食之；一二年中，一鄉中輒為之儉。傅子曰：時太原發冢破棺，棺中有一生婦人，將出與語，生人也。送之京師，問其本事，不知也。視其冢上樹木可三十歲，不知此婦人三十歲常生於地中邪？將一朝欻生，偶與發冢者會也？







Second Year, Spring, Second Moon [234 Mar 18 – Apr 15], Jǐwèi [234 Mar 21], Tàibái crossed Yínghuò. Guǐyǒu [234 Apr 4], Edict said: “Caning as government punishment is to correct negligence, but recently as a result there have been many innocent deaths. Thus reduce the systems of caning rods, written in law.” Third Moon [234 Apr 16 – May 15], Gēngyín [234 Apr 21], the Duke of Shānyáng died, the Emperor wore mourning clothes and held mourning, sending envoy Holding Stave to manage the funeral arrangements. Jǐyǒu [234 May 10], Great Amnesty. Summer, Fourth Moon [234 May 16 – Jun 14], great epidemic. Chónghuá Hall burned down. Bǐngyín [234 May 27], Edict on the relevant managers to use Grand Offering to report and sacrifice to Emperor Wén’s Temple. Posthumously named the Duke of Shānyáng as Hàn Xiào-Xiàn Huángdì, buried by Hàn Rituals. [16]



二年春二月乙未，太白犯熒惑。癸酉，詔曰：「鞭作官刑，所以糾慢怠也，而頃多以無辜死。其減鞭杖之制，著于令。」三月庚寅，山陽公薨，帝素服發哀，遣使持節典護喪事。己酉，大赦。夏四月，大疫。崇華殿災。丙寅，詔有司以太牢告祠文帝廟。追諡山陽公為漢孝獻皇帝，葬以漢禮。〔一〕










[16] Xiàn-dì zhuàn states: The Emperor changed dress and led the various ministers to weep for him, sending Envoy Holding Stave as Acting Excellency over the Masses the Minister of Ceremonies Hé Qià for condolence sacrifices, also sending Envoy Holding Stave as Acting Excellency of Works the Minister of Agriculture Cuī Lín to supervise the funeral affairs. Edict said: “Overall in the affairs and customs of the Five Emperors, Zhòngní enthusiastically praised the towering and sweeping achievements of Yáo and Shùn, believing that abdication succession then was the exemplary affair of great sages. The Duke of Shānyáng deeply understood the fate of Heaven’s blessings forever completing, abdicating the throne to Wén Huángdì [Cáo Pī] to obey Heaven’s Mandate. The Former Emperor mandated that the Duke enact Hàn’s Standard Calendar, Suburb Heaven Sacrifices to Ancestors by the Rituals of Heaven’s Son, in reporting affairs to not call himself a servant; these were the principles of Shùn serving Yáo. In the past when Fàngxūn [Yáo] died, the Four Seas mourned him as for father and mother, restraining the eight tones, which shows that the rituals of the funeral and burial were the same as for the ruler. Now relevant managers memorialize for the funeral rituals to be those for the vassal lord kings; how is this the legacy systems of antiquity and the utmost intentions of the Former Emperor? Now posthumously title the Duke as Hàn Xiào-Xiàn Huángdì.” Sent the Grand Commandant to provide one Grand Offering to report and sacrifice to Wén Huángdì’s temple, stating: “[I, Cáo] Ruì have heard that in Ritual, return to the roots and learn from antiquity, do not forget the origins, and therefore the lords of former dynasties honored the honorable and were close with the close, all having esteem. Now the Duke of Shānyáng lying ill relinquished his state, the relevant managers suggested that the rituals of the funeral proceedings observe those for the vassal lord kings. [I, Cáo] Ruì consider that the Duke of Shānyáng in the past understood that Heaven’s Mandate forever completed on himself, deeply observed that the calendar calculations were upon Your Sagely Body, transferred the blessings and abdicated the throne, honoring our rule of the people; this then was a situation of Táo Táng’s exemplary virtue. In Huángchū at the completion of the receiving, you mandated that the Duke in his state enact Hàn’s Standard Calendar, Suburb Heaven Sacrifices to Ancestors, Rituals and Music Systems to all follow Hàn’s old ways; these also were the principles of Shùn and Yǔ in the Míngtáng. Above examining to the origins, in the distant establishments of the Imperial standards, in granting prosperity by maintaining humility, none are as clear as this. Overall a son takes continuing will and inheriting teachings as filial piety, a servant takes matching commands and respectfully narrating as loyalty, and therefore the Shī states ‘Not for urgency in this, only for pursuing filial piety,’ the Shū states ‘The predecessor received the mandate, now do not forget the great achievement.’ Dare [I, Cáo] Ruì not respectfully serve beautiful canon to manifest my Imperial father’s divine spirit? Now posthumously title the Duke of Shānyáng as Xiào-Xiàn Huángdì, confer and bestow the Ruler’s Seal and Ribbon. Mandate the Excellency over the Masses and Excellency of Works Holding Stave to offer condolence sacrifices and manage the funeral, the Minister of Staff and Minister Herald as assistants, the General Architect and Restoring Soil General to build and complete the tomb, with installation of the hundred officials and various clerks, chariots and flags and uniforms and insignia and funeral and burial rituals and ceremonies all by the Hàn dynasty’s former practices. The expenses for supplying the various officials for the funeral and burial, are all assigned to the Minister of Agriculture. Establish his successor as the Duke of Shānyáng, to continue the Three Lineages and forever be Wèi’s Guest. ” Thereupon the bestowal conferment said: “Alas, in the past the August Heavens sent down disaster on Hàn, causing the traitor minister Dǒng Zhuó to spread his vicious brutality, burning down the capital city, stealing away the Great Carriage. At that time the Six Directions were like clouds billowing, treacherous opportunists like flames rising. The Emperor from the western capital reached out only to seek stability, arriving at this Luò city. Consulting the sagely and worthy, he then changed his carriage direction, again moving to Xǔchāng, with Wǔ Huángdì [Cáo Cāo] to depend on.
