Suì was at Xuánxiāo, the Imperial brigades began to campaign, until at Chúnwěi, ten and eight years, the crowds of bandits were exterminated, the nine regions all governed, thus the Emperor in remembrance of the achievements, blessed this Wèi state, greatly opening its territory realm. Then reaching to Wén Huángdì [Cáo Pī], a comprehensive sage broad and profound, benevolent sound spreading and flowing, softening the distant and able to draw close, differing customs turning to righteousness, heavenly essence presented blessings, earthly spirit emitted radiance, inspecting to Yùhéng, embracing the calendar calculations, followed the course of etiquette, able to satisfy the Emperor’s heart. Thus looking up to venerate the seven governments, looking down to investigate the five canons, not selecting the plan of the Sìyuè, not waiting for the nomination of everyone’s bestowal, distantly supported by the divine intelligence, serving Heaven he abdicated the throne. The blessings reach to Our person, succeeding and continuing the vast enterprise. Overall hearing that in the past of Emperor Yáo, the foremost and harmonious were already nominated, the vicious clans were not yet exiled, raising Shùn to manage the hundred affairs, only afterward were the hundred affairs timely ordered, inside pacified and outside completed, conferring the throne in the Míngtáng, withdrawing to end Heaven’s blessings, therefore he was able to have virtue above the hundred kings, achievements higher than the highest mountains. From the past reaching to now, it has completely passed through seven dynasties, years reaching to three thousand, and the great fate comes again, assigning mandate and setting merits, setting me as the ruler of the people, building and establishing the Imperial standards. Remembering Chóngguāng and continuing Xiánchí, succeeding Sháo and Xià, surpassing the distant legacies of the various lords, distancing from the shamed virtues of Shāng and Zhōu, it can be said to be a high and clear glorious ending, the exemplary flourishing of shining enlightenment and vast exploits. If it is not Hàn and Wèi with Heaven and Earth joining in virtue, with the Four Seasons joining in faith, actions harmonizing humanity and divinity, aligned to above and below, then what would be able to reach to this? We consider that Xiào-Xiàn lived long but not forever, reverently follow his deathbed mandate, investigate the canon practices, respectfully narrate my Imperial father’s former spirit’s legacy intentions, express esteem by vast posthumous title, to respectfully complete his sagely beauty, to make clear the greatness of a rare correspondence, to pass on the glory that will for a hundred million years not decay. If the soul yet has awareness, enjoy this vast glory. Alas the Sorrow!” Eighth Moon [234 Sep 11 – Oct 10], Rénshēn [234 Sep 30], buried at Shānyáng state, the tomb called Shànlìng, installed a park and village. On the day of the burial, the Emperor wore mourning vest, cap, and sash, weeping with grief. The successor grandson the Marquess of Guìshì village [Liú] Kāng succeeded and was established as Duke of Shānyáng.



〔一〕　獻帝傳曰：帝變服，率群臣哭之，使使持節行司徒太常和洽弔祭，又使持節行大司空大司農崔林監護喪事。詔曰：「蓋五帝之事尚矣，仲尼盛稱堯、舜巍巍蕩蕩之功者，以為禪代乃大聖之懿事也。山陽公深識天祿永終之運，禪位文皇帝以順天命。先帝命公行漢正朔，郊天祀祖以天子之禮，言事不稱臣，此舜事堯之義也。昔放勛殂落，四海如喪考妣，遏密八音，明喪葬之禮同於王者也。今有司奏喪禮比諸侯王，此豈古之遺制而先帝之至意哉？今諡公漢孝獻皇帝。」使太尉具以一太牢告祠文帝廟，曰：「叡聞夫禮也者，反本脩古，不忘厥初，是以先代之君，尊尊親親，咸有尚焉。今山陽公寢疾棄國，有司建言喪紀之禮視諸侯王。叡惟山陽公昔知天命永終於己，深觀曆數允在聖躬，傳祚禪位，尊我民主，斯乃陶唐懿德之事也。黃初受終，命公于國行漢正朔，郊天祀祖禮樂制度率乃漢舊，斯亦舜、禹明堂之義也。上考遂初，皇極攸建，允熙克讓，莫朗于茲。蓋子以繼志嗣訓為孝，臣以配命欽述為忠，故詩稱『匪棘其猶，聿追來孝』，書曰『前人受命，茲不忘大功』。叡敢不奉承徽典，以昭皇考之神靈。今追諡山陽公曰孝獻皇帝，冊贈璽紱。命司徒、司空持節弔祭護喪，光祿、大鴻臚為副，將作大匠、復土將軍營成陵墓，及置百官群吏，車旗服章喪葬禮儀，一如漢氏故事；喪葬所供群官之費，皆仰大司農。立其後嗣為山陽公，以通三統，永為魏賓。」於是贈冊曰：「嗚呼，昔皇天降戾于漢，俾逆臣董卓，播厥凶虐，焚滅京都，劫遷大駕。于時六合雲擾，姦雄熛起。帝自西京，徂唯求定，臻茲洛邑。疇咨聖賢，聿改乘轅，又遷許昌，武皇帝是依。歲在玄枵，皇師肇征，迄于鶉尾，十有八載，群寇殲殄，九域咸乂。惟帝念功，祚茲魏國，大啟土宇。爰及文皇帝，齊聖廣淵，仁聲旁流，柔遠能邇，殊俗向義，乾精承祚，坤靈吐曜，稽極玉衡，允膺曆數，度于軌儀，克厭帝心。乃仰欽七政，俯察五典，弗采四嶽之謀，不俟師錫之舉，幽贊神明，承天禪位。祚（建）〔逮〕朕躬，統承洪業。蓋聞昔帝堯，元愷既舉，凶族未流，登舜百揆，然後百揆時序，內平外成，授位明堂，退終天祿，故能冠德百王，表功嵩嶽。自往迄今，彌歷七代，歲暨三千，而大運來復，庸命厎績，纂我民主，作建皇極。念重光，紹咸池，繼韶夏，超群后之遐蹤，邈商、周之慚德，可謂高朗令終，昭明洪烈之懿盛者矣。非夫漢、魏與天地合德，與四時合信，動和民神，格于上下，其孰能至於此乎？朕惟孝獻享年不永，欽若顧命，考之典謨，恭述皇考先靈遺意，闡崇弘諡，奉成聖美，以章希世同符之隆，以傳億載不朽之榮。魂而有靈，嘉茲弘休。嗚呼哀哉！」八月壬申，葬于山陽國，陵曰禪陵，置園邑。葬之日，帝制錫衰弁絰，哭之慟。適孫桂氏鄉侯康，嗣立為山陽公。







That Moon, Zhūgě Liàng set out Yé valley, garrisoned Wèinán. Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng led the various armies to resist him. Edict on [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng: “Only fortify to resist and defend to blunt their edge. They in advancing will not obtain their ambition, in retreating will have no one to battle. If they station for long then their provisions will be exhausted, plundering will have no gains, and then they will certainly flee. Fleeing and then pursuing them, using the rested to deal with the exhausted, is the way to total victory.” [17]



是月，諸葛亮出斜谷，屯渭南，司馬宣王率諸軍拒之。詔宣王：「但堅壁拒守以挫其鋒，彼進不得志，退無與戰，久停則糧盡，虜略無所獲，則必走矣。走而追之，以逸待勞，全勝之道也。」〔一〕










[17] Wèishì Chūnqiū states: [Zhūgě] Liàng had repeatedly sent envoys to pass letters, and also delivered women’s headdress ornaments to anger [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng was about to go out to battle, Xīn Pí holding stave presented Edict to restrain [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng and the army officials on down, and thus it stopped. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng met with [Zhūgě] Liàng’s envoy, only asking about his resting and eating and how complex or simple were his affairs, not asking about military affairs. The envoy replied saying: “Excellency Zhūgě rises early and sleeps late, punishments of twenty [cane strokes] and above he all personally oversees. What he eats does not exceed a few shēng.” [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng said: “[Zhūgě] Liàng’s body is already dead; how can he last long?”



〔一〕　魏氏春秋曰：亮既屢遣使交書，又致巾幗婦人之飾，以怒宣王。宣王將出戰，辛毗杖節奉詔，勒宣王及軍吏已下，乃止。宣王見亮使，唯問其寢食及其事之煩簡，不問戎事。使對曰：「諸葛公夙興夜寐，罰二十已上，皆親覽焉；所啖食不過數升。」宣王曰：「亮體斃矣，其能久乎？」







Fifth Moon [234 Jun 15 – Jul 13], Tàibái during daytime seen. Sūn Quán entered to occupy Cháo lake’s mouth, heading toward Héféi Xīnchéng, also sent officers Lù Yì and Sūn Sháo to each lead over ten thousand men to enter the Huái and Miǎn. Sixth Moon [234 Jul 14 – Aug 12], Campaigning East General Mǎn Chǒng advanced the army to resist them. [Mǎn] Chǒng wished to evacuate Xīnchéng’s defenders, to draw the rebels to Shòuchūn, the Emperor did not listen, saying: “In the past Hàn Guāng-Wǔ sent soldiers to separately occupy Lüèyáng, in the end defeating Wěi Áo. The Former Emperor in the east installed Héféi, in the south defended Xiāngyáng, in the west hardened Qíshān. That the rebels in coming at once were defeated below these three cities is because the land must be contested. Even if [Sūn] Quán attacks Xīnchéng, he certainly is unable to take it. Order the various officers to firmly defend. I will personally go campaign against him. By the time I arrive I fear [Sūn] Quán will have fled.” Autumn, Seventh Moon [234 Aug 13 – Sep 10], Rényín [234 Aug 31], the Emperor personally drove dragon boat on eastern campaign. [Sūn] Quán attacked Xīnchéng, General Zhāng Yǐng and others resisted and defended in fierce battle. The Emperor’s army had not yet arrived by several hundred lǐ, [Sūn] Quán escaped and fled, [Lù] Yì and [Sūn] Sháo and the rest also retreated. The various ministers believed that as the General-in-Chief [Sīmǎ Yì] was still with Zhūgě Liàng locked together without resolution, the Chariot Carriage could go west to visit Cháng’ān. The Emperor said: “[Sūn] Quán has fled, [so Zhūgě] Liàng’s courage is broken. With the General-in-Chief to restrain him, I have no concerns.” Therefore advanced the army to visit Shòuchūn, noting the various officers’ achievements, enfeoffing and rewarding each on distinct basis. Eighth Moon [234 Sep 11 – Oct 10], Jǐwèi [234 Sep 17], greatly exhibition of the soldiers, feasted the Six Armies, sent envoy Holding Stave to reward and feast Héféi’s and Shòuchūn’s various armies. Xīnsì [234 Oct 9], went back to Xǔchāng Palace.



五月，太白晝見。孫權入居巢湖口，向合肥新城，又遣將陸議、孫韶各將萬餘人入淮、沔。六月，征東將軍滿寵進軍拒之。寵欲拔新城守，致賊壽春，帝不聽，曰：「昔漢光武遣兵縣據略陽，終以破隗囂，先帝東置合肥，南守襄陽，西固祁山，賊來輒破於三城之下者，地有所必爭也。縱權攻新城，必不能拔。敕諸將堅守，吾將自往征之，比至，恐權走也。」秋七月壬寅，帝親御龍舟東征，權攻新城，將軍張穎等拒守力戰，帝軍未至數百里，權遁走，議、韶等亦退。群臣以為大將軍方與諸葛亮相持未解，車駕可西幸長安。帝曰：「權走，亮膽破，大將軍以制之，吾無憂矣。」遂進軍幸壽春，錄諸將功，封賞各有差。八月己未，大曜兵，饗六軍，遣使者持節犒勞合肥、壽春諸軍。辛巳，行還許昌宮。

三年春正月戊子，以大將軍司馬宣王為太尉。己亥，復置朔方郡。京都大疫。丁巳，皇太后崩。乙亥，隕石于壽光縣。三月庚寅，葬文德郭后，營陵于首陽陵澗西，如終制。〔一〕










[18] Gù Kǎizhī’s Qǐméng zhù states: In Wèi’s time there was someone who opened the burial mound of a Zhōu king, finding a sacrificed buried alive woman. 〔一〕　顧愷之啟蒙注曰：魏時人有開周王冢者，得殉葬女子，經數日而有氣，數月而能語；年可二十。送詣京師，郭太后愛養之。十餘年，太后崩，哀思哭泣，一年餘而死。







At that time, greatly repaired Luòyáng Palace, raising Zhāoyáng and Tàijí Halls, building Zǒngzhāng Watchtower. The Hundred Surnames lost farming time, upright ministers Yáng Fù and Gāotáng Lóng and others each repeatedly made harsh remonstrations. Although [Cáo Ruì] did not listen, he always exceptionally tolerated them. [19]



是時，大治洛陽宮，起昭陽、太極殿，築總章觀。百姓失農時，直臣楊阜、高堂隆等各數切諫，雖不能聽，常優容之。〔一〕










[19] Wèi lüè states: That year raised Tàijí’s various Halls, built Zǒngzhāng Watchtower, height over ten zhàng, setting a soaring fèng [statue] at its top. Also in Fānglín Garden raised a pond reservoir, rowing boats of singers. Also to the north of the lines of Halls, established Eight Workshops, the various Crafts Women in sequence residing within, the Noble Ladies and Ladies and above transferred to the south attachment, their salary ranks in imitation to the numbers of the Hundred Officials. The Emperor always roamed and feasted in the interior, and thus selected women who knew calligraphy and who could be trusted, six people, to be Female Secretariat Writers, having them manage and review the exterior’s memorialized reports, able to draft approvals. From the Noble Ladies on down to Secretariat Protectors, with those provided to the Lateral Courts for washing and sweeping, and those trained in performance and song, each were in the thousands. Connected and drew in the Gǔ river water past Jiǔlóng Hall’s front, with jade wells and silk railings, a toad mouth [statue] receiving, a divine dragon [statue] spitting it out. Employed Academic Scholar Mǎ Jūn to build a south-pointing carriage and a water-powered puppet show. At the start of the year established the large beasts and sea creatures performances and acrobatic horse-riding performances, prepared following the systems of Hàn’s Western Capital. Built screens beyond Chānghé’s various gates and towers. Heir-Apparent’s Resident Zhāng Mào believed that Wú and Shǔ were repeatedly mobilizing, the various officers out on campaign, but the Emperor was greatly raising Palace Residences, leaving his attention on playthings and decorations, giving out bestowments without moderation, the treasury emptied and exhausted, and also noted that the daughters of soldiers that had previously already been married off to be the wives of officials and civilians were being seized back to be paired with soldiers, with the ability to use slaves as substitution, and also there was selection of those with beauty to enter the Lateral Courts, and so sent up a letter of remonstration that said: “Your Servant in prostration read the Edict letter, that the daughters of soldiers that were married to non-soldiers were to be entirely registered and taken back to be paired with battle soldiers. This truly is appropriate for a temporary expedience, but not good for overall cultivation. Your Servant requests to explain it. Your Majesty is the child of Heaven. The Hundred Surnames and officials and civilians also are Your Majesty’s children. By Ritual, the bestowments on noble men and on petty men are not on the same day, in order to distinguish the noble and the lowly. The sorts as officials are noble men, the soldiers are petty men. Now seizing from that to give to this, is also no different from seizing an elder brother’s wife to be wife of a younger brother, a bias in the love of a father and mother. Also the Edict letter permits the use of a slave comparable in age and appearance as the wife to be a substitution, and therefore the wealthy then overturn their houses and exhaust their wealth, the poor borrow loans on credit, expensively buying slaves to ransom their wives. County officials are using the claim of pairing to soldiers but are in fact sending them to the Lateral Courts, the ugly then sent out to be given to the soldiers. Those obtaining the women will not necessarily have pleased hearts, but those losing wives certainly will have mournful expressions, some destitute some anxious, all not obtaining their wishes. The lords who possessed Heaven’s Under but did not obtain the pleased hearts of the myriad surnames, rarely were they not in grave danger. Moreover the army brigades on the exterior are several tens of millions of men, the costs of one day are not merely a thousand gold, raising the taxation on Heaven’s Under to provide for these labors, still they are not provided for. Furthermore there are women in the Palace courts who are not personnel and not registered, the families of the Jiāofáng and the mother dowager are wildly given rewards and bestowments, in the transactions of the interior and the exterior, the costs are half that of the army. In the past Hàn Emperor Wǔ favored immortals and trusted in technicians, dug the ground into seas, piled soil into mountains, relying only on that Heaven’s Under was unified at that time, with none daring to oppose him. From since the decline and chaos onward it has been forty to fifty years, horses never taking off saddles, soldiers never taking off armor, in every battle engagement, blood flows into red fields, the sounds of the pained wails of the wounded to the present have not yet ended, yet still strong bandits are at the borders, plotting to endanger the Wèi House. Your Majesty is not conscientious in considering the esteeming of frugality or pondering how to calm Heaven’s Under, but instead devotes attention to extravagance, the Central Secretariat Crafters only make play things, exhibited in the Rear Garden, establishing pans for dew collecting. This truly pleases the observations of your ears and eyes, but it also is sufficient to encourage the hearts of the bandits and enemies. A pity! To abandon the frugality of Yáo and Shùn and enact the extravagant affairs of Hàn Wǔ, Your Servant humbly believes that Your Majesty should not do so. May Your Majesty decisively send down Edict, that of the myriad affairs those without benefit and having harm are all to be eliminated, and have the eliminated costs of things without benefit be generously bestowed on the hungry and cold of the fathers and mothers and wives and children of the officers and soldiers, inquire into what the people suffer from and eliminate what they abhor, fill the granaries, mend the armor and weapons, with respect and care oversee Heaven’s Under. In this way, the Wú rebels will face while bound, the Shǔ caitiffs cart coffins, without waiting for punishment yet themselves submit, and the road to Grand Peace can be calculated in days and waited for. Your Majesty can be without laboring thought of beyond the seas, the army brigades rest high, the battle soldiers stand by. Now the various Excellencies all hold their tongues, but the reason Your Servant does not dare not proffer crude speech, is that Your Servant in the past sent up ‘Essential Reports,’ the Cavaliers memorialized Your Servant’s letter, believing the ‘Hearing Remonstration’ chapter to be good, and Edict said: ‘It is,’ promoting Your Servant to be Heir-Apparent’s Resident. Moreover, Your Servant wrote ridicule of servants of men being unable to admonish and criticize, now for there to be a situation of being able to remonstrate and yet Your Servant to not remonstrate, this is to have written empty absurdities and be unable to speak. Your Servant’s years are fifty, always I fear to reach death with nothing to repay the state, and therefore I throw myself to sacrifice life presumptuously to be heard, may Your Majesty investigate it.” The letter was delivered, the Superior looked back to his Left and Right and said: “Zhāng Mào is relying on being from the same homeland.” The matter was given to the Cavaliers and nothing more. [Zhāng] Mào appellation Yànlín was a Pèi man.



〔一〕　魏略曰：是年起太極諸殿，築總章觀，高十餘丈，建翔鳳於其上；又於芳林園中起陂池，楫櫂越歌；又於列殿之北，立八坊，諸才人以次序處其中，貴人夫人以上，轉南附焉，其秩石擬百官之數。帝常游宴在內，乃選女子知書可付信者六人，以為女尚書，使典省外奏事，處當畫可，自貴人以下至尚保，及給掖庭灑掃，習伎歌者，各有千數。通引穀水過九龍殿前，為玉井綺欄，蟾蜍含受，神龍吐出。使博士馬均作司南車，水轉百戲。歲首建巨獸，魚龍曼延，弄馬倒騎，備如漢西京之制，築閶闔諸門闕外罘罳。太子舍人張茂以吳、蜀數動，諸將出征，而帝盛興宮室，留意於玩飾，賜與無度，帑藏空竭；又錄奪士女前已嫁為吏民妻者，還以配士，既聽以生口自贖，又簡選其有姿色者內之掖庭，乃上書諫曰：「臣伏見詔書，諸士女嫁非士者，一切錄奪，以配戰士，斯誠權時之宜，然非大化之善者也。臣請論之。陛下，天之子也，百姓吏民，亦陛下之子也。禮，賜君子小人不同日，所以殊貴賤也。吏屬君子，士為小人，今奪彼以與此，亦無以異於奪兄之妻妻弟也，於父母之恩偏矣。又詔書聽得以生口年紀、顏色與妻相當者自代，故富者則傾家盡產，貧者舉假貸貰，貴買生口以贖其妻；縣官以配士為名而實內之掖庭，其醜惡者乃出與士。得婦者未必有懽心，而失妻者必有憂色，或窮或愁，皆不得志。夫君有天下而不得萬姓之懽心者，尠不危殆。且軍師在外數千萬人，一日之費非徒千金，舉天下之賦以奉此役，猶將不給，況復有宮庭非員無錄之女，椒房母后之家，賞賜橫興，內外交引，其費半軍。昔漢武帝好神仙，信方士，掘地為海，封土為山，賴是時天下為一，莫敢與爭者耳。自衰亂以來，四五十載，馬不捨鞍，士不釋甲，每一交戰，血流丹野，創痍號痛之聲，于今未已。猶彊寇在疆，圖危魏室。陛下不兢兢業業，念崇節約，思所以安天下者，而乃奢靡是務，中尚方純作玩弄之物，炫燿後園，建承露之盤，斯誠快耳目之觀，然亦足以騁寇讎之心矣。惜乎，舍堯舜之節儉，而為漢武之侈事，臣竊為陛下不取也。願陛下沛然下詔，萬幾之事有無益而有損者悉除去之，以所除無益之費，厚賜將士父母妻子之饑寒者，問民所疾而除其所惡，實倉廩，繕甲兵，恪恭以臨天下。如是，吳賊面縛，蜀虜輿櫬，不待誅而自服，太平之路可計日而待也。陛下可無勞神思於海表，軍師高枕，戰士備員。今群公皆結舌，而臣所以不敢不獻瞽言者，臣昔上要言，散騎奏臣書，以聽諫篇為善，詔曰：『是也』，擢臣為太子舍人；且臣作書譏為人臣不能諫諍，今有可諫之事而臣不諫，此為作書虛妄而不能言也。臣年五十，常恐至死無以報國，是以投軀沒命，冒昧以聞，惟陛下裁察。」書通，上顧左右曰：「張茂恃鄉里故也。」以事付散騎而已。茂字彥林，沛人。

秋七月，洛陽崇華殿災，八月庚午，立皇子芳為齊王，詢為秦王。丁巳，行還洛陽宮。命有司復崇華，改名九龍殿。冬十月己酉，中山王兗薨。壬申，太白晝見。十一月丁酉，行幸許昌宮。〔一〕










[20] Wèishì Chūnqiū states: That year, Zhāngyè prefecture’s Shāndān county’s Jīn mountain’s Xuán creek overflowed and gushed forth a treasure stone with a diagram on its back, shaped like a tortoise, width one zhàng six chǐ, length one zhàng seven chǐ one cùn, circumference five zhàng eight cùn, standing to the creek’s west. It had stone horses of seven, one with an immortal riding it, one with a bridle, five having shape but not fully completed. There was a jade box closed and covered at the front, above having jade characters, jade rings of two, semicircle of one. A qílín was on the east, fèng bird on the south, white tiger on the west, sacrificial ox on the north, horses from the center spreading in lines on the four sides, colors all pale white. Its south had five characters stating: “Up Up Three Heaven Kings.” It also said: “Following great metal, great suppression department, Metal merely takes it, metal established center, great metal horse of one at center, great fortune opens longevity, this horse Jiǎyín follows water.” Altogether the “center” characters were six, the “metal” characters were ten. Also there were symbols resembling the Eight Trigrams and the asterisms and comets.
Shìyǔ states: Also there was one rooster image.
Sōushénjì states: Previously, during the reigns of Hàn Yuán and Chéng, a serviceman of foresight had a report saying when Wèi’s years have harmony, there would be an opening stone to the west by over three thousand lǐ, fastened to five horses, inscription saying: ‘great suppression department.’ Reaching to when Wèi first rose, Zhāngyè’s Liǔgǔ had an opening stone, first seen during Jiàn’ān, taking shape during Huángchū, inscription appearing during Tàihé, the circumference seven xún, center height one rén, dark blue material and white markings, images of dragon horse, lín deer, fènghuáng, immortals, clear and bright and all distinct. This entire situation was a sign of Wèi’s and Jìn’s succession and rise. Reaching to Jìn’s Tàishǐ Third Year [267], Zhāngyè Administrator Jiāo Shèng sent up report that in comparing the original chart left in the prefecture to the present stone inscription, the written characters had some not the same, and solemnly prepared another chart to send up. According to that writing there were images of five horses, one having a man with flat top cap, holding a halberd and riding it, one had something resembling a horse in shape but not complete, the characters had ‘metal,’ had ‘center,’ had ‘Marshal-in-Chief,’ had ‘king,’ had ‘great fortune,’ had ‘standard,’ had ‘open longevity,’ and one complete phrasing saying: ‘Metal will take it.’
Hàn Jìn Chūnqiū states: Dīchí county’s large Liǔgǔ’s mouth in the night had a shock wave flooding out, its sound like thunder, at dawn there was a dark blue stone standing in the river, length one zhàng six chǐ, height eight chǐ, white stone drawings on it, forming thirteen horses, one ox, one bird, images of the Eight Trigrams and jade rings, all protruding out, its inscription stating “great suppression department, fitting water center, Jiǎyín.” The Emperor hated the ‘suppression’ and had it chiseled into “calculation,” with dark blue stone obstructing it. In the night the white stone filled it up. Reaching to Jìn’s beginning, its inscription became increasingly bright and clear, the horse images all glowing through like jade.



〔一〕　魏氏春秋曰：是歲張掖郡刪丹縣金山玄川溢涌，寶石負圖，狀象靈龜，廣一丈六尺，長一丈七尺一寸，圍五丈八寸，立于川西。有石馬七，其一仙人騎之，其一羈絆，其五有形而不善成。有玉匣關蓋於前，上有玉字，玉玦二，璜一。麒麟在東，鳳鳥在南，白虎在西，犧牛在北，馬自中布列四面，色皆蒼白。其南有五字，曰「上上三天王」；又曰「述大金，大討曹，金但取之，金立中，大金馬一匹在中，大（告）〔吉〕開壽，此馬甲寅述水」。凡「中」字六，「金」字十；又有若八卦及列宿孛彗之象焉。世語曰：又有一雞象。搜神記曰：初，漢元、成之世，先識之士有言曰，魏年有和，當有開石於西三千餘里，繫五馬，文曰「大討曹」。及魏之初興也，張掖之柳谷，有開石焉，始見於建安，形成於黃初，文備於太和，周圍七尋，中高一仞，蒼質素章，龍馬、麟鹿、鳳皇、仙人之象，粲然咸著，此一事者，魏、晉代興之符也。至晉泰始三年，張掖太守焦勝上言，以留郡本國圖校今石文，文字多少不同，謹具圖上。按其文有五馬象，其一有人平上幘，執戟而乘之，其一有若馬形而不成，其字有「金」，有「中」，有「大司馬」，有「王」，有「大吉」，有「正」，有「開壽」，其一成行，曰「金當取之」。漢晉春秋曰：氐池縣大柳谷口夜激波涌溢，其聲如雷，曉而有蒼石立水中，長一丈六尺，高八尺，白石畫之，為十三馬，一牛，一鳥，八卦玉玦之象，皆隆起，其文曰「大討曹，適水中，甲寅」。帝惡其「討」也，使鑿去為「計」，以蒼石窒之，宿昔而白石滿焉。至晉初，其文愈明，馬象皆煥徹如玉焉。
